literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在5年期间,共有11.3%(499/4414)的<2岁儿童因实验室确诊的RSV感染住院被转入ICU。ICU 队列研究患儿的中位年龄为3.3个月,而非ICU样本的中位年龄为7.1个月。 [10.1071/pu25136]
这些观察结果支持,但并未确立,一个模型:即严重的下呼吸道RSV感染可能通过活化或其组织微环境来为后续对过敏原的过度反应奠定基础。 [10.1093/ajrcmb/aanag207]
B.D.E.1和B.D.E.1.2占主导地位,占所有序列的86.0%。所有谱系中均存在保守的G:I252T取代,且预测存在糖基化差异。 [10.1016/j.ijmmb.2026.101316]
作者得出结论,母体疫苗接种可有效将抗体转移给婴儿,而尼塞韦单抗可显著减少下呼吸道感染、住院、ICU入院和严重RSV疾病的发生,具有良好的安全性,表明对这两种策略的疗效和安全性存在广泛共识。 [10.24875/bmhime.m26000139]
RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统的发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023)一致;而HMPV则表现出中间分布。 [PMCID:PMC13645514]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Over a 5-year period, 11.3% (499/4414) of children hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (3.3 months) compared with the non-ICU sample (7.1 months). [10.1071/pu25136]

These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. [10.1093/ajrcmb/aanag207]

B.D.E.1 and B.D.E.1.2 predominated, comprising 86.0% of sequences. The conserved G:I252T substitution was present across all lineages, with predicted glycosylation differences. [10.1016/j.ijmmb.2026.101316]

The authors conclude that maternal vaccination effectively transfers antibodies to the infant and that nirsevimab markedly reduces lower respiratory tract infection, hospitalisation, ICU admission and severe RSV disease, with a favorable safety profile, indicating broad agreement on the efficacy and safety of both strategies. [10.24875/bmhime.m26000139]

RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution. [PMCID:PMC13645514]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
在5年期间,共有11.3%(499/4414)的<2岁儿童因实验室确诊的RSV感染住院被转入ICU。ICU 队列研究患儿的中位年龄为3.3个月,而非ICU样本的中位年龄为7.1个月。 [10.1071/pu25136]。
这些观察结果支持,但并未确立,一个模型:即严重的下呼吸道RSV感染可能通过活化或其组织微环境来为后续对过敏原的过度反应奠定基础。 [10.1093/ajrcmb/aanag207]。
B.D.E.1和B.D.E.1.2占主导地位,占所有序列的86.0%。所有谱系中均存在保守的G:I252T取代,且预测存在糖基化差异。 [10.1016/j.ijmmb.2026.101316]。
作者得出结论,母体疫苗接种可有效将抗体转移给婴儿,而尼塞韦单抗可显著减少下呼吸道感染、住院、ICU入院和严重RSV疾病的发生,具有良好的安全性,表明对这两种策略的疗效和安全性存在广泛共识。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

Over a 5-year period, 11.3% (499/4414) of children hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (3.3 months) compared with the non-ICU sample (7.1 months).

These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. [10.1093/ajrcmb/aanag207].

papers.title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network, 2019–2023
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, involving 4414 children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, comprising all ICU admitted and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients.
analysis.methods: The study involved collecting data on RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years, with the main outcome measures being characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions. Factors associated with ICU admission were identified using multivariate logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Over a 5-year period, 11.3% (499/4414) of children hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (3.3 months) compared with the non-ICU sample (7.1 months).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted preventative programs for high-risk groups, including Indigenous children, those born prematurely, and children with cardiac disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted before the implementation of government-funded immunisation programs, which may limit its ability to predict the impact of such programs. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential for unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a multi-centre, retrospective cohort analysis of RSV hospitalisations among children under 2 years in Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network from 2019 to 2023. It found that 11.3% of RSV hospitalisations required ICU admission, with younger age, prematurity, Indigenous identity, and cardiac disease identified as significant risk factors. The results highlight the need for targeted preventative strategies for high-risk populations. However, the study's retrospective design and lack of data on immunisation programs limit its ability to fully assess the impact of future interventions. The findings provide moderate evidence for informing public health strategies related to RSV surveillance and prevention.

papers.title_zh: 悉尼儿童医院网络中<2岁儿童呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疾病增强型呼吸道合胞病毒和监测描述,2019–2023年
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

papers.title: Pulmonary ILC2 Priming as a Link Between Severe Early-Life RSV Bronchiolitis and Asthma
papers.abstract: Abstract Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved. Airway samples from infants with severe RSV disease and experimental models show robust IL-33 responses and pulmonary group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) activation during acute infection. Additionally, neonatal IL-33 and allergen-rechallenge studies demonstrate that ILC2s can persist and acquire memory-like properties. These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. Beyond limited interferon control and prolonged epithelial injury, which may amplify IL-33/ST2 signaling during a developmental window when long-lived lung ILC2 populations are established, we focus on additional candidate mechanisms that could sustain this priming. These include metabolic pathways governing glycolysis, lipid utilization, iron uptake, and mitochondrial function; epigenetic mechanisms involving chromatin remodeling and histone or DNA modifications; and neuroimmune signals that regulate ILC2 activation and recall. Direct evidence that RSV induces durable, cell-intrinsic metabolic, epigenetic, or neuroimmune reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is currently lacking. Longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer of RSV-experienced versus control ILC2s are needed to test this model. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies now provide an opportunity to determine whether preventing severe early-life RSV disease alters airway immune programming and subsequent asthma risk.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the link between severe early-life RSV bronchiolitis and asthma by investigating the role of pulmonary ILC2 priming. It highlights that severe RSV disease may prime ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens, but direct evidence of durable reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is lacking. The research suggests that mechanisms such as metabolic pathways, epigenetic changes, and neuroimmune signals could sustain this priming. The study also notes that maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies offer potential avenues to assess whether preventing severe RSV disease can alter airway immune programming and reduce asthma risk. The evidence is moderate, as the study provides supporting observations but lacks direct confirmation of the priming mechanism.

papers.title: Outbreak of BA genotype-derived RSV-B lineages in Northeast India: Molecular epidemiology and phylogenetic insights from Dibrugarh, 2022
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness in children, but molecular data from Northeast India remain limited. We investigated an RSV-B outbreak among 239 children aged <5 years in Dibrugarh, Assam, during November-December 2022. RSV-B was detected in 67 (28.0%) samples by real-time RT-PCR. G-gene sequencing of 43 isolates and phylogenetic analysis identified three BA genotype-derived lineages: B.D.E.1 (48.8%), B.D.E.1.2 (37.2%), and B.D.4.1.1 (14.0%). B.D.E.1 and B.D.E.1.2 predominated, comprising 86.0% of sequences. The conserved G:I252T substitution was present across all lineages, with predicted glycosylation differences. These findings provide evidence of RSV-B lineage circulation in Northeast India.

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿、老年人以及患有心肺合并症或免疫功能低下的个体下呼吸道疾病的主要原因。最近的进展使得分层预防成为可能,通过用于婴儿保护的母体 疫苗接种、用于新生儿和特定幼儿的长效单克隆抗体以及用于老年人的 疫苗。然而,监测 中的不平等、季节性驱动的时间安排以及负担能力和交付方面的挑战(特别是在低收入和中等收入国家)阻碍了公平的采用。这篇社论强调了重点人群,综合了当前的证据和政策方向,并概述了融资、采购和综合母婴保健服务方面的可行杠杆,以加速获得服务,使 RSV 预防成为紧迫且可实现的全球卫生优先事项。

6Hospital Universitario Dr. José Eleuterio González, Universidad Autónoma de Nuevo León, Monterrey, Nuevo León; 7Infectious Diseases Unit, Hospital Médica Sur, Mexico City; 8Health Supplies Procurement, Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social, Mexico City; 9Asociación Mexicana de Vacunología, Mexico City; 10Department of Infectious Diseases, Unidad Médica de Alta Especialidad, Hospital de Gineco Pediatría 48, Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social, León, Guanajuato; 11Research Laboratory for Infectious and Parasitic Diseases, Hospital Infantil de México Federico Gómez, Mexico City; 12Department of Pediatric Infectious Diseases, Antiguo Hospital Civil de Guadalajara Fray Antonio Alcalde, Guadalajara, Jalisco; 13Department of Infectious Diseases, Instituto Nacional de Pediatría, Mexico City; 14Department of Pediatrics, Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social, Irapuato, Guanajuato; 15Asociación Mexicana de Infectología Pediátrica, Mexico City; 16Infectious Diseases Unit, Hospital Español, Mexico City; 17Laboratory of Inborn Errors of Metabolism, Instituto Nacional de Pediatría, Mexico City; 18Academia Mexicana de Pediatría, Mexico City, Mexico Boletín Médico del Hospital Infantil de México REVIEW ARTICLE Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the leading causes of acute lower respiratory tract infection, bronchiolitis, pneu­ monia, and hospitalization among infants and young children, with the highest risk of severe disease observed in infants younger than six months, preterm infants, and children with bronchopulmonary dysplasia, congenital heart disease, immuno­ compromising conditions, and other underlying comorbidities. In Mexico, available evidence demonstrates a substantial cli­ nical burden and a predominant seasonal circulation from September to March. In recent years, the development of novel preventive strategies has transformed the approach to RSV prevention, particularly through maternal immunization with a bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine and passive immunoprophylaxis with long-acting monoclonal antibodies. This position statement from the Mexican Academy of Pediatrics reviews the epidemiological, clinical, and real-world effectiveness evidence regarding currently available strategies for the prevention of RSV infection in the pediatric population. Maternal vaccination between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation promotes transplacental antibody transfer and provides protection to infants during the first months of life. Monoclonal antibodies, particularly nirsevimab, have demonstrated significant reductions in lower respiratory tract infection, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, and severe RSV-associated disease, with a favorable safety profile. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/). 212 Bol Med Hosp Infant Mex (Eng). 2026;83(4) Epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an RNA virus belonging to the family Pneumoviridae and consists of 2 genotypes (A and B). RSV is specific to and patho­ genic in humans and infects cells of the respiratory tract. In 2025, RSV was the leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infections, causing 3.6 million hospitalizations annually in children younger than 5 years and significantly increasing the risk of mortality in older adults with comorbidities. Most children infected with RSV have mild symptoms, but some develop severe disease (bronchiolitis or pneumonia). RSV is estimated to cause more than 100 000 deaths annually in children younger than 5 years, and more than 97% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries.1 Recent epidemiologic data highlight the predomi­ nance of RSV-A and the high mortality burden in low- and middle-income countries, accounting for more than 95% of pediatric deaths worldwide.2 The epidemiology of RSV has attracted increasing interest in recent years, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, which dramatically altered the transmission dynamics of various respiratory viruses. The pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syn­ drome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) altered seasonal RSV patterns worldwide, with a substantial decrease observed during 2020 in all countries. Atypical out­ breaks and delays in the onset of seasonal peaks were reported in several regions, suggesting accumulated susceptibility in the pediatric population. Following the pandemic, RSV showed signs of returning to prepan­ demic seasonal trends, with a more consistent recovery observed in countries in the Southern Hemisphere than in equatorial regions. The duration of RSV sea­ sonality ranged from 4 to 32 weeks across countries. Predominantly negative correlations between RSV and integrating maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibody immunoprophylaxis, initially prioritizing high-risk infants and gra­ dually expanding coverage to all susceptible infants. Implementation should consider efficacy, safety, cost-effectiveness, operational feasibility, equity, and timely access. Keywords: Respiratory syncytial virus. Maternal vaccination. Monoclonal antibodies. Recommendations. Prevention. Infants. Posicionamiento de la Academia Mexicana de Pediatría sobre estrategias para la prevención de la infección por virus sincicial respiratorio en la población pediátrica de México Resumen El virus sincicial respiratorio (VSR) constituye una de las principales causas de infección respiratoria aguda baja, bronquio­ litis, neumonía y hospitalización en niños, con mayor riesgo de gravedad en menores de seis meses, prematuros, pacientes con displasia broncopulmonar, cardiopatías congénitas, inmunocompromiso y otras comorbilidades. En México, la evidencia disponible muestra una carga clínica relevante y una estacionalidad predominante de septiembre a marzo. El desarrollo de nuevas estrategias preventivas ha transformado el abordaje del VSR, particularmente mediante la vacunación materna con vacuna bivalente de proteína F prefusión y la inmunoprofilaxis pasiva con anticuerpos monoclonales de acción prolongada. El presente posicionamiento de la Academia Mexicana de Pediatría revisa la evidencia epidemiológica, clínica y de efecti­ vidad en vida real sobre las estrategias disponibles para la prevención de la enfermedad por VSR en población pediátrica. La vacunación materna entre las 32 y 36 semanas de gestación permite la transferencia transplacentaria de anticuerpos y confiere protección al lactante durante los primeros meses de vida. Por su parte, los anticuerpos monoclonales, especialmente el nirsevimab, han demostrado reducciones significativas en infección respiratoria baja, hospitalización, ingreso a cuidados intensivos y enfermedad grave asociada a VSR, con un perfil de seguridad favorable. Con base en la carga de enfermedad, la estacionalidad nacional, la disponibilidad de productos preventivos y las condiciones del sistema de salud mexicano, la Academia Mexicana de Pediatría propone una estrategia complementaria y progresiva que integre vacunación materna e inmunoprofilaxis con anticuerpos monoclonales, priorizando inicialmente a lactantes de alto riesgo y ampliando de manera gradual la cobertura hacia todos los lactantes susceptibles. Palabras clave: Virus sincicial respiratorio. Vacuna materna. Anticuerpos monoclonales. Recomendaciones. Prevención. Lactantes. 213 R.M. Wong-Chew et al. AMP position statement on RSV prevention SARS-CoV-2 circulation were observed in most countries, suggesting possible mechanisms of viral interference. RSV subtype A predominated in most countries after 2022.3 RSV transmission occurs primarily through direct contact and respiratory droplets, facilitating its spread in crowded settings such as schools, daycare centers, and hospitals. A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the burden of hospital-acquired RSV infection in children found a pooled incidence rate of 10.86 cases per 1000 person-years among hospitalized pediatric patients. The mortality rate was 11.34 deaths per 1000 person-years.4 This study highlights that hospital-acquired RSV has a case-fatality rate of 13.30%, significantly higher than that of community-acquired RSV, which usually ranges from 0% to 1.7%. Hospital-acquired RSV accounts for approximately 15.57% of all RSV hospitalizations and 22.48% of all health care-associated infections in pedi­ atric patients. This infection is a “serious and under­ recognized” cause of death; therefore, strengthening infection control and prevention strategies in hospital settings is important.4 In Latin America and the Caribbean, RSV represents a substantial disease burden. A recent meta-analysis including 156 studies from the region, mainly from Brazil (25%), Colombia (14.5%), and Argentina (13.8%), found that the highest pooled prevalence was esti­ mated among patients younger than 1 year (58%), with type A and B prevalences of 52% and 34%, respec­ tively. The incidence of RSV lower respiratory tract infection was 15 per 100 symptomatic infants younger than 2 years, with an intensive care unit (ICU) admis­ sion rate of 42%. The RSV case fatality rate was 0.6% in patients younger than 2 years, 3% in children aged 0-5 years, and 23% in high-risk patients older than 65 years.5 In Mexico, RSV is the leading cause of lower respi­ ratory tract infection and hospitalization in infants and preschool-aged children. Studies conducted at several hospitals show that RSV causes approximately 40%- 44% of hospitalizations for lower respiratory tract infec­ tion in children younger than 5 years.6,7 In a multicenter study conducted at 7 hospitals in Mexico, RSV caused 38% of pneumonia cases in children younger than 14 years during the pandemic (2021-2023) and 28% after the pandemic (2023-2025).8 At a pediatric referral hospital (2004-2008), 75% of isolated viruses were RSV; 91% of patients required hospitalization and 16% required mechanical ventilation. Among preterm infants, the RSV hospital­ ization rate during the first year of life was 9.4% in infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia, 5.9% in those with congenital heart disease, and 2.6% in preterm infants without comorbidities.9 A recent national study (2023-2024) found severe disease (hospitalized bronchiolitis/pneumonia) in 21% of 2022 children with confirmed RSV infection.10 Risk factors Prematurity, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and con­ genital heart disease are the main risk factors for RSV lower respiratory tract infection. RSV is more frequent and severe in infants younger than 12 months, with risk decreasing as age increases.7 Newborns aged 1-28 days and patients with comorbidities such as heart disease, immunosuppression, chronic lung disease, primary or acquired immunodeficiencies (eg, HIV), Down syn­ drome, cancer, malformations, or neurologic diseases have at least twice the risk of requiring hospitalization and a 6- to 8-fold higher risk of ICU admission.6 Seasonality RSV usually causes seasonal epidemics, with out­ breaks generally occurring between October and May in the Northern Hemisphere, between May and September in the Southern Hemisphere, and during rainy periods in tropical regions.3,4 In Mexico, epidemiologic studies reported by several authors, including studies conducted in different regions of the country, show a seasonal pattern begin­ ning in September and ending in March, including regions with tropical climates such as the Yucatán Peninsula.8,11-13 (Fig. 1). RSV is one of the most frequent pathogens causing substantial morbidity and mortality in children. These findings underscore the importance of continuous sur­ veillance, the need to optimize prevention strategies, and implementation of early diagnostic techniques to improve prevention. Several antiviral treatments are under development, and important advances have been made in vaccine research and production. An important approach is passive immunization with mono­ clonal antibodies and maternal vaccination, which have been shown to be effective in preventing severe infec­ tions in at-risk populations. Continuous epidemio­ logic surveillance of RSV, together with research and development of effective prevention strategies, is cru­ cial to addressing its public health impact. 214 Bol Med Hosp Infant Mex (Eng). 2026;83(4) Figure 1. RSV seasonality. Monthly relative index constructed from several national reports. In each study, the months corresponding to onset, increase, peak, decline, and absence or minimal RSV circulation were identified. When articles provided monthly values, these were transformed to a common scale from 0 to 5 using relative normalization, assigning the maximum value in each series a score of 5. When studies did not provide exact monthly values but described the circulation season or months of greatest activity, a semiquantitative ordinal score was assigned: 0 for absent or minimal activity, 1 for residual activity, 2 for low activity, 3 for moderate increase or decline, 4 for high activity, and 5 for the month or period with the highest reported activity. The scale ranges from 0 to 5, where 0 indicates minimal or undetected activity and 5 indicates the relative peak of activity. The index does not represent direct population incidence but rather a visual synthesis of the temporal patterns reported in Mexican studies using heterogeneous metrics.8,11,13 (figure created with ChatGPT). Evidence from clinical trials has demonstrated significant effi­ cacy; however, recently generated real-world evidence has confirmed its impact under diverse programmatic and population conditions, with consistent results across different geographic regions and health care systems. One of the first real-world effectiveness studies was conducted in the United Kingdom using a multicenter test-negative case-control design, including 537 moth­ er-infant pairs. In Mexico, available evidence demonstrates a substantial cli­ nical burden and a predominant seasonal circulation from September to March. Although methodological details of the review are not provided, the authors report consensus that both interventions are effective and safe, reducing severe disease and hospitalisation. No specific controversies or evidence gaps are identified in the supplied text. The authors propose a complementary national strategy that integrates maternal immunisation and nirsevimab use, coupled with continued surveillance of RSV seasonality and real‐world effectiveness to guide implementation in Mexico’s pediatric population.

papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致婴幼儿和儿童急性下呼吸道感染、毛细支气管炎、肺炎和住院的主要原因之一,其中6个月以下婴儿、早产儿以及患有支气管肺发育不良、先天性心脏病、免疫抑制状况及其他基础合并症的儿童面临最严重的疾病风险。在墨西哥,现有证据表明RSV感染具有显著的临床负担,并且主要在9月至3月期间呈现季节性流行。近年来,新型预防策略的发展改变了RSV预防的方法,特别是在通过双价前融合F蛋白疫苗进行母体免疫接种以及使用长效单克隆抗体进行被动免疫预防方面。墨西哥儿科学会发布的这一立场声明回顾了目前针对儿童群体RSV感染预防策略的流行病学、临床和真实世界效果证据。在妊娠32至36周期间进行的母体疫苗接种可促进抗体通过胎盘转移,并在婴儿出生后的最初几个月内提供保护。单克隆抗体,特别是尼塞韦单抗,已被证明可显著降低下呼吸道感染、住院、重症监护病房入院以及严重RSV相关疾病的发病率,且具有良好的安全性。基于疾病负担、国家季节性特征、预防产品的可获得性以及墨西哥医疗体系的特性,墨西哥儿科学会建议采用一种互补且逐步推进的国家策略。

papers.title: Risk Factors for Hypoxia, Mechanical Ventilation, and Mortality in Lung Transplant Recipients Hospitalized with Respiratory Syncytial Virus: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Lung transplant (LT) recipients are at high risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, but predictors of worse outcomes remain poorly defined. Methods Retrospective multicenter cohort study of adult LT recipients hospitalized with PCR-confirmed RSV infection between January 2016 and December 2019. Clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of outcomes, while Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk factors for mortality. Results 155 LT recipients were included. Median age was 61 years, RSV occurred a median of 14 months post-transplant. Risk factors for hypoxic respiratory failure were baseline oxygen use [OR 4.8, (1.29–23.93)] and lower respiratory tract symptoms [OR 3.74, (1.49–10.18)]. Older age increased the risk of mechanical ventilation [OR 1.06, (1.02–1.12)], while oral ribavirin was associated with reduced risk [OR 0.34, (0.14–0.82)]; this association was attenuated when oral and inhaled ribavirin were combined into a single exposure variable [OR 0.77, (0.22–2.66)]; oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality [HR 5.27, (0.68–40.83)]. Secondary bacterial or fungal infections occurred in 33.5%, associated with prior mechanical ventilation. Lung function declined significantly post-RSV infection, with nearly half experiencing >10% decrease in FEV1. Ninety-day all-cause mortality was 7.7%, with mechanical ventilation independently associated with death [HR 7.79, (2.47–24.60)]. Conclusions RSV infection in LT recipients is associated with high morbidity, graft function decline, and mortality. The association between older age and severe outcomes suggests the importance of preventive strategies in this high-risk population.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter international cohort study investigated risk factors for hypoxia, mechanical ventilation, and mortality in lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The study analyzed clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes within 90 days of infection. Results showed that baseline oxygen use and lower respiratory tract symptoms were significant predictors of hypoxic respiratory failure. Older age was linked to an increased risk of mechanical ventilation, while oral ribavirin showed a reduced risk, though this association weakened when combined with inhaled ribavirin. Oral ribavirin was not associated with reduced 90-day mortality. The study highlights the importance of preventive strategies for older lung transplant recipients and the need for further research on ribavirin's efficacy. Limitations include the retrospective design and potential biases, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定肺移植受者住院期间发生呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染时缺氧、机械通气和死亡率的风险因素,因为预测较差预后的因素仍不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2016年1月至2019年12月期间,对因PCR确认的RSV感染而住院的成年肺移植受者进行了回顾性多中心队列研究研究。
elements_zh.methods: 分析了临床特征、治疗以及90天内的结局。使用逻辑回归模型确定结局的预测因素,采用Cox比例风险模型评估死亡率的风险因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 共纳入155例肺移植受者。缺氧性呼吸衰竭的风险因素包括基线吸氧使用[OR 4.8,(1.29–23.93)]和下呼吸道症状[OR 3.74,(1.49–10.18)]。年龄较大与机械通气风险增加相关[OR 1.06,(1.02–1.12)],而口服利巴韦林与风险降低相关[OR 0.34,(0.14–0.82)];当将口服和吸入利巴韦林合并为单一暴露变量时,该关联减弱[OR 0.77,(0.22–2.66)];口服利巴韦林与90天内死亡率无显著关联[HR 5.27,(0.68–40.83)]。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 年龄较大与严重结局的关联提示在这一高危人群中预防策略的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了需要针对特定人群实施预防策略,并突显了监测肺移植受者RSV感染后严重结局的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为回顾性研究,基于医院记录,这可能引入偏倚并限制研究结果的普遍适用性。由于这些局限性,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 肺移植(LT)受者感染呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)后出现严重并发症的风险较高,但预测较差预后的因素仍不明确。方法 回顾性多中心队列研究研究,纳入2016年1月至2019年12月期间因PCR确认的RSV感染而住院的成年肺移植受者。分析了临床特征、治疗以及90天内的结局。使用逻辑回归模型确定结局的预测因素,采用Cox比例风险模型评估死亡率的风险因素。结果 共纳入155例肺移植受者。中位年龄为61岁,RSV感染发生在移植后中位14个月。缺氧性呼吸衰竭的风险因素包括基线吸氧使用[OR 4.8,(1.29–23.93)]和下呼吸道症状[OR 3.74,(1.49–10.18)]。年龄较大与机械通气风险增加相关[OR 1.06,(1.02–1.12)],而口服利巴韦林与风险降低相关[OR 0.34,(0.14–0.82)];当将口服和吸入利巴韦林合并为单一暴露变量时,该关联减弱[OR 0.77,(0.22–2.66)];口服利巴韦林与90天内死亡率无显著关联[HR 5.27,(0.68–40.83)]。33.5%的受者发生了继发性细菌或真菌感染,与之前机械通气相关。RSV感染后肺功能显著下降,近一半的受者FEV1下降超过10%。90天内所有原因的死亡率发生率为7.7%,机械通气与死亡独立相关[HR 7.79,(2.47–24.60)]。结论 肺移植受者RSV感染与高发病率、移植物功能下降和死亡率相关。年龄较大与严重结局的关联提示在这一高危人群中预防策略的重要性。

papers.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.full_text: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. As a tertiary referral center, the cohort is likely enriched for more severe disease and for cases referred from primary and secondary facilities; this referral pattern, and the resulting limit on generalizability to primary care, is revisited in the Discussion (Section 4.6).Eligible participants were children aged 0–18 years hospitalized with a clinical diagnosis of LRTI between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025, from whom a respiratory specimen was submitted for routine viral testing. LRTI was defined clinically, following the 2019 Chinese Pediatric Society guideline for community-acquired pneumonia (Subspecialty Group of Respiratory Diseases, 2019), as cough or fever (axillary temperature ≥38 °C) together with at least one of: tachypnoea, wheezing, crackles on auscultation, or imaging evidence of pneumonia or bronchiolitis. This definition captures the clinical syndromes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis and excludes isolated upper respiratory tract infection. We excluded children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease, congenital airway malformations, documented immunodeficiency, active malignancy, or concurrent infection by pathogens outside the predefined six-virus panel. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. For viruses prone to subclinical carriage, chiefly HRV and HBoV, a detection was considered clinically causative only when the tNGS reporting algorithm assigned a pathogenicity Class A grade, the clinical picture matched the corresponding viral syndrome, and other plausible infectious causes had been clinically excluded (residual misclassification risk for these two viruses is discussed in Section 4.6). For descriptive analyses, children were stratified a priori into four age categories: infants (<1 year), toddlers (1–2 years), preschoolers (3–5 years) and school-aged children (≥6 years). All records were de-identified before analysis. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital (approval number 2024-LXKY-023); written informed consent was waived given the retrospective design and full de-identification of the dataset.2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. It is generated by an integrated scoring system that combines normalized read counts (reads per million, RPM), the breadth of genome coverage achieved across the targeted regions, and species-level annotation of pathogenicity against a curated reference database; Class A is assigned to organisms that meet the pre-specified RPM and coverage criteria for a clinically significant pathogen. The numerical RPM and coverage cut-offs behind the grade are proprietary to the assay vendor and are not released to the ordering laboratory; we are therefore unable to report them, and the grade as issued was the only form in which this information was available to us. Grading was prospective in the sense that it was performed by the clinical laboratory at the time the routine diagnostic report was issued and used for patient care, and the research team did not re-adjudicate the classifications retrospectively. No Class A detection was subsequently excluded on the grounds of clinical mismatch, because the Class A flag served as an inclusion criterion for the six-virus panel rather than as the sole determinant of clinical causality; for HRV and HBoV, the additional clinical adjudication described in Section 2.1 was applied instead.The full panel detects a broader range of organisms than the six viruses analyzed here. Common bacterial pathogens reported by the full panel include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus; the atypical pathogens include Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae; and respiratory viruses outside the six-virus panel, including parainfluenza viruses, seasonal coronaviruses and SARS-CoV-2, are likewise covered. Consistent with the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2.1, a child in whom any of these organisms was reported concurrently with one of the six target viruses was excluded from the cohort at screening rather than merely omitted from the analysis; the cases analysed here are therefore restricted to children whose Class A detections fell entirely within the six-virus panel. We restricted the present analysis to the six respiratory viruses (HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, covering both influenza A and B, and HMPV) flagged at the highest pathogenicity grade (Class A), for three reasons. First, these six viruses are the pathogens for which pathogen-specific climatic drivers are most biologically plausible and best characterized, allowing direct comparison with prior lagged-climate studies (Baker et al., 2019; Li et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2021). Second, restricting to Class A calls minimizes the inclusion of low-confidence or incidental detections. Third, bacterial and atypical pathogens are subject to different detection biases (for example, antibiotic pretreatment and colonization) and different climate–transmission mechanisms, and were therefore outside the scope of this analysis. Co-infections, defined as concurrent Class A detection of two or more of the six target viruses in the same specimen, were identified and are described in Section 2.4.2.3Meteorological dataMonthly city-wide meteorological summaries for Tianjin from January 2023 to December 2025 (n = 36 months) were obtained from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau and comprised mean atmospheric pressure (hPa), mean wind speed (m/s), mean air temperature (°C), mean relative humidity (%), precipitation (mm) and mean daily sunshine duration (hours). Routine quality assurance included unit verification and column-order auditing across reporting periods. The meteorological series was time-aligned with the monthly aggregated viral case counts before analysis.We used monthly rather than daily or weekly data because the records available from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau for this study period were supplied at monthly resolution; daily or weekly city-wide summaries were not accessible for the full 2023–2025 window. Finer (for example, weekly) resolution would allow more precise estimation of short-lag effects and is standard in DLNM-based climate–infection studies (Gasparrini et al., 2010; Li et al., 2025); we discuss this resolution constraint further in Section 4.6.2.4Statistical analysisCategorical data are presented as counts (percentages) and compared between groups with Pearson’s χ2 test; the assumption of an equal sex ratio was tested with the exact binomial test, and inter-pathogen age differences with the Kruskal–Wallis test. Daily case records were aggregated to monthly totals and merged with the meteorological time series. Yates’ continuity correction was applied to 2 × 2 comparisons.Co-infections were tabulated separately from the mono-infection pathogen spectrum. The primary pathogen-spectrum analysis (case counts, proportions, and demographic and specimen-type distributions in Section 3.1) attributes each specimen to a single, mutually exclusive pathogen row, so the per-pathogen counts in Table 1 sum to the total of 2,597 virus-positive cases; co-infection structure itself (pairwise combinations, and multiplicity) is tabulated separately, with each co-infected specimen contributing to every virus it carried, and is described in Section 3.4.Table 1Demographic and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI cases by pathogen.PathogenN (% of all positive)Male, n (%)Female, n (%)Sex p-valueAge, median (IQR), yLower respiratory tract specimen, n (%)HRV796 (30.7)471 (59.2)325 (40.8)<0.0014.0 (2.0–6.0)660 (82.9)ADV692 (26.6)425 (61.4)267 (38.6)<0.0016.0 (3.0–8.0)485 (70.1)RSV536 (20.6)304 (56.7)232 (43.3)0.0023.0 (1.0–4.0)454 (84.7)HBoV313 (12.1)179 (57.2)134 (42.8)0.0132.0 (1.0–4.0)277 (88.5)IFV155 (6.0)83 (53.5)72 (46.5)0.425.0 (2.0–7.0)123 (79.4)HMPV105 (4.0)66 (62.9)39 (37.1)0.0114.0 (1.8–6.0)74 (70.5)Pathogen counts are mutually exclusive per specimen (see Section 2.4), so the column totals sum to 2,597. Co-infected specimens, in which two or more Class A viruses were detected concurrently, are tabulated separately in Section 3.4, where each such specimen contributes to the count of every virus it carried; those pairwise counts are not reflected in the totals above. Sex p-values are from the exact binomial test against a 50:50 null; age is median (IQR) in years; Lower respiratory tract specimen = sputum or BALF.Pathogen–climate co-variation was screened with Spearman’s rank correlation (ρ) on the full monthly series and re-examined within meteorological seasons (spring, March–May; summer, June–August; autumn, September–November; winter, December–February).Lagged meteorological effects were examined in two complementary ways. Second, lag-specific relative risks (RR) were derived from quasi-Poisson GLMs with a log link (Bhaskaran et al., 2013; Gasparrini, 2011; Imai et al., 2015) of the form log(μt) = α + β × Xt−L, where μt is the expected monthly case count in month t and Xt−L the meteorological exposure shifted back by L months (L = 0, 1, ..., 6). Under the null hypothesis, roughly six of the 126 fits would be expected to reach p<0.05 by chance, and a Bonferroni-corrected threshold would fall at p<0.0004. full_text_sections.abstract: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities.

full_text_sections.results: 3Results3.1Overall pathogen distribution and demographicsAcross 36 surveillance months we identified 2,597 virologically confirmed pediatric LRTI cases. HRV was the most frequently detected virus (796 cases, 30.7%), followed by ADV (692, 26.6%), RSV (536, 20.6%), HBoV (313, 12.1%), IFV (155, 6.0%) and HMPV (105, 4.0%) (Figure 2A; Table 1). Sputum was the predominant specimen type for HRV, RSV, HBoV, HMPV and IFV. The proportion of cases sampled from the lower airway (sputum or BALF) likewise differed across pathogens (χ2 = 73.7, df = 5, p < 0.001), ranging from 70.1% for ADV and 70.5% for HMPV to 88.5% for HBoV (Table 1). ADV was more evenly distributed across specimen types, with BALF (35.4%) and sputum (34.7%) contributing similar shares and nasopharyngeal swabs a further 29.6%, giving ADV a markedly higher BALF share than the other five viruses (Figure 2B). Annual case counts rose from 188 in 2023 to 1,027 in 2024 and 1,382 in 2025 (Figure 2C). The 2023 figures warrant particular caution on this account. The assay reached full clinical implementation only in the fourth quarter of that year (Section 2.2), so the 188 cases recorded in 2023 almost certainly under-represent circulation during the early post-pandemic period relative to 2024 and 2025, when testing volume was broadly stable. Subsequent analyses therefore emphasize pathogen composition, age distribution and seasonal timing, which are far less sensitive to testing volume than absolute case counts.Figure 2Overall pathogen spectrum and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, 2023–2025. (A) Case distribution across the six viral pathogens, ranked by prevalence. (B) Specimen-type composition by pathogen. (C) Annual case burden, stacked by pathogen.Grouped bar and stacked bar chart panel showing (A) case numbers and percentages for six pathogens, (B) specimen composition by pathogen, and (C) annual case burden from 2023 to 2025. HRV and ADV have the highest positive cases, sputum is the most common specimen, and total case burden increases each year, with pathogen contribution shown by color.Two features of the assay bound the influence of testing volume without removing it. All six viruses sit on a single multiplex panel and are screened simultaneously in every specimen, so no virus could be tested more often than another, and a change in ordering volume alters which children were tested rather than which viruses were sought. What this cannot exclude is a shift in case mix: if tNGS was ordered preferentially for more severely ill children, and if the pathogen spectrum of severe admissions differs from that of milder ones, composition will move with ordering practice. The markedly higher BALF share of ADV (Figure 2B) is consistent with such a gradient, and the point is developed in Section 4.6.Boys predominated for HRV (59.2%, p<0.001), ADV (61.4%, p<0.001), RSV (56.7%, p=0.002), HBoV (57.2%, p=0.013) and HMPV (62.9%, p=0.011), whereas IFV showed a balanced sex ratio (53.5% male, p=0.42) (Table 1; Figure 3A). Although IFV was the only virus without a male excess, a χ2 test for heterogeneity across the six pathogens did not reach significance (χ2 = 5.77, df = 5, p = 0.33), and neither did the comparison of IFV against the other five viruses combined (χ2 = 1.68, df = 1, p = 0.20). The balanced ratio for IFV is therefore better read as a failure to demonstrate a male excess in the smallest of the larger groups (n = 155) than as evidence of a genuinely different sex distribution.Figure 3Demographic composition of pediatric viral LRTI by pathogen. (A) Sex distribution, with binomial-test significance markers. (B) Age (years) by pathogen (median, IQR), with jittered individual data points overlaid. Significance markers: *p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001; ns = not significant.Bar chart on the left shows male and female sex distribution for six pathogens with males consistently higher for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, and HMPV; differences denoted by statistical significance symbols. Boxplot on the right displays age distribution in years for each pathogen with medians, interquartile ranges, and data points, indicating variation in median ages by pathogen.Age distributions differed sharply across pathogens (Kruskal–Wallis H = 372.7, p < 0.001; Figure 3B). Infants and toddlers carried most HBoV (median 2.0 [IQR 1.0–4.0] years) and RSV (3.0 [1.0–4.0]) cases; preschoolers were the main group for HRV (4.0 [2.0–6.0]) and HMPV (4.0 [1.8–6.0]); ADV predominated in school-aged children (6.0 [3.0–8.0]), while IFV spanned the older preschool-to-school-age range (median 5.0 [2.0–7.0]) (Table 1; Figure 3B).3.2Temporal distributionMonthly time-series of the six pathogens (Figure 4A) showed strong but pathogen-specific seasonality. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all reached their annual maxima in December, consistent with the cold, dry continental winter being the dominant transmission season in northern China. The December peak of late 2024 (about 400 positive cases that month) was the largest monthly count of the surveillance period, with a smaller but still notable winter peak in December 2025. HBoV behaved differently, showing a single summer maximum in July. ADV showed a secondary peak in late spring (April–May), and HRV and ADV together produced the broadest seasonal envelope (March–December) of any pathogen. The seasonal heatmap (Figure 4B) summarizes these patterns: each virus shows at least one clearly defined month-of-year peak, and HBoV is the only virus to peak in a warm-season month (July). Because the heatmap is normalized row-wise, color intensity for each pathogen is scaled to its own monthly range; the visual prominence of a peak for a low-incidence pathogen (for example, HMPV) therefore does not indicate the same absolute case count as for a high-incidence pathogen (for example, HRV).Figure 4Temporal distribution of pediatric viral LRTI, 2023–2025. (A) Stacked monthly case counts by pathogen. (B) Seasonal heatmap of mean monthly cases by pathogen; cell shading is normalized row-wise so that each pathogen’s twelve-month profile can be read on a comparable scale.Stacked bar chart and heatmap visualizing monthly viral pathogen detections from January 2023 to December 2025. The chart (panel A) shows case counts for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, and HMPV, with peaks observed between late 2024 and early 2025. The heatmap (panel B) presents mean cases per month for each virus, highlighting increased relative intensity for most pathogens in November and December, with values labeled within cells and a scale indicating intensity from low (yellow) to high (red).3.3Seasonal and meteorological analyses3.3.1Overall pathogen–climate correlationsOverall Spearman rank correlations (Figure 5A; Table 2) showed a significant positive correlation between HBoV and temperature (ρ = +0.34, p = 0.04). ADV (ρ = +0.32, p = 0.06), HRV (ρ = +0.28, p = 0.10) and RSV (ρ = +0.24, p = 0.16) showed positive but non-significant trends. IFV and HMPV showed non-significant negative correlations with temperature (ρ = −0.27 and −0.05). Relative humidity followed a similar pattern: HBoV (+0.33), ADV (+0.30) and HRV (+0.28) correlated positively, whereas IFV (−0.29) and HMPV (−0.23) correlated negatively. Wind speed produced predominantly negative correlations across the six viruses, strongest for HBoV (−0.32), ADV (−0.30) and HRV (−0.29).Figure 5Pathogen–meteorology correlations. (A) Overall Spearman ρ between monthly case counts and six meteorological variables; the color bar is fixed at the symmetric range −1 to +1 to allow direct comparison across panels. (C–F) Season-stratified Spearman ρ for the three core exposures across spring, summer, autumn and winter, using the same −1 to +1 symmetric scale. Cell labels show ρ with significance markers (*p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001).Composite figure with six panels. Panel A is a heatmap showing Spearman correlati…
full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionIn this three-year, single-center cohort we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, a megacity on the North China Plain, and quantified how closely monthly viral activity tracks ambient weather. To our knowledge, the dataset is unusual for northern China in spanning six respiratory viruses, including the comparatively under-surveyed HRV, HBoV and HMPV, over the full 2023–2025 post-pandemic rebound window, with a complete and time-matched monthly meteorological record.4.1Principal epidemiological featuresAcross the six viruses, HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading causes of pediatric LRTI, and each pathogen carried a well-defined demographic profile. Age and sex stratification confirmed recognized biological gradients. RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution. The older age skew of IFV fits its epidemiology in temperate regions, where school-aged children are the principal drivers of seasonal influenza transmission and the group in which symptomatic infection is most readily recognized, in contrast to the infant and toddler predominance of RSV and HBoV (Feng et al., 2024; Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The male predominance for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV and HMPV, but not IFV, echoes prior pediatric LRTI cohorts and may reflect sex differences in innate immunity and behavior (Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The strong age-group × pathogen association reinforces the need for an explicitly age-stratified surveillance framework.The six pathogens also fell into two distinct seasonal groups. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all peaked in December, during the cold, dry continental winter, whereas HBoV stood apart with an isolated July maximum—the only warm-season peak of the panel. HRV additionally displayed the broadest seasonal envelope, circulating from March to December, consistent with fundamentally endemic, weakly seasonal behavior. Because the rise in absolute case counts partly reflects expanding testing volume rather than incidence (Section 3.1), the interpretation that follows rests on pathogen composition, age structure and seasonal timing rather than on raw counts.4.2Interpretation in the post-pandemic contextThese patterns are best read against, rather than directly measured against, pre-pandemic Chinese pediatric surveillance, since our cohort describes the post-pandemic period without a matched pre-pandemic Tianjin comparator. Several multi-center Chinese studies contrasting pre-pandemic (2018–2019) with post-pandemic (2023 onward) cohorts have reported a broadly consistent post-pandemic pattern: higher overall pathogen positivity and mixed-infection rates, a higher proportion of severe presentations, and shifts in the relative ranking, seasonal timing and age distribution of individual pathogens (Cui et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). In Shanghai, post-pandemic test positivity rose markedly relative to 2019, with both RSV and ADV increasing and RSV’s onset shifting earlier into August, ahead of its conventional winter season (Liu et al., 2025); other Chinese cohorts spanning the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic phases have likewise documented altered seasonal timing and age-distribution shifts for RSV, ADV and rhinovirus after non-pharmaceutical interventions were relaxed (Cui et al., 2024).Interpreted against this backdrop, our Tianjin observations show both continuities and departures. HRV’s endemic, weakly seasonal circulation—reflected in its leading position and broad March–December envelope—appears to have been less perturbed by the pandemic and its aftermath than that of the more strongly seasonal viruses. By contrast, the convergence of five of the six viruses onto a single sharp December peak is consistent with the compressed, intensified post-pandemic winter surge described elsewhere in China, plausibly reflecting the accumulated immunity debt from population-level exposure gaps in 2020–2022 (Cohen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024) superimposed on the resumption of normal contact patterns. HBoV departed most sharply from this winter pattern, peaking instead in summer; to our knowledge, such an isolated warm-season peak has not been prominently reported as a post-pandemic phenomenon elsewhere in China. Whether it reflects a genuine post-pandemic shift in HBoV’s seasonal niche or a feature specific to Tianjin’s continental climate cannot be resolved with a single-center, single-period dataset, and we return to its biological and clinical significance in Section 4.4.4.3Climate-driven lagged effectsThe unadjusted and seasonally adjusted analyses answer different questions, and reading them together guards against a common pitfall in climate–infection studies. In the unadjusted analysis (Table 3), IFV appeared the most climate-responsive virus, with antecedent humidity and temperature aligning with later case counts, in keeping with the recognized seasonal phasing of influenza in temperate climates (Deyle et al., 2016; Kudo et al., 2019; Lowen et al., 2007; Lowen and Steel, 2014). Once seasonality and secular trend were held constant in the unified model, however, these IFV associations disappeared (Table 5). This does not mean that IFV has no climatic drivers. Rather, because ambient temperature and humidity in Tianjin themselves follow an almost perfect annual sinusoid, they are nearly collinear with the sine–cosine seasonal terms of the unified model; for a virus as tightly locked to the annual cycle as influenza (77.5% of deviance explained by season and trend alone), the model simply cannot separate the effect of “season” from that of “temperature” or “humidity.” The most that can be concluded is that, at the present monthly resolution, IFV shows no climatic association detectable independently of the seasonal cycle itself.The seasonally adjusted model instead isolated RSV and HMPV as the only viruses with climate associations independent of shared seasonality (Table 5): RSV tracked temperature and wind speed at short lags, while HMPV tracked temperature positively and humidity inversely, although its low case counts make these estimates imprecise and hypothesis-generating. HRV, ADV and HBoV showed no independent lagged signal, indicating that at monthly resolution their seasonal envelopes are not accompanied by a detectable climate effect beyond the annual cycle. This null result should not be read as evidence of climatic insensitivity. For these three viruses the seasonal-plus-trend baseline itself explained comparatively little of the monthly deviance (HRV 41.5%, HBoV 28.6%, ADV 17.1%; Table 4), so a large share of the variation in their case counts is left unaccounted for by season, trend and weather combined. Residual variation of that magnitude widens the standard errors, and with 36 monthly observations spanning three seasonal cycles only associations of substantial size could reach significance. A modest but real climate effect would probably have escaped detection here, and the finding is better described as uninformative for HRV, ADV and HBoV than as negative. The contrast between the two analyses carries the key methodological lesson: lagged climate associations in surveillance data can be interpreted only after seasonality has been accounted for.These post-pandemic patterns can be read against the pre-pandemic national baseline of Xu et al. (2021), who modelled a seven-virus panel—five of them shared with our own—across 81 sentinel hospitals in 22 Chinese provinces (2009–2013) and ranked the meteorological factors by climate region. For the temperate north, to which Tianjin belongs, three points agree wit…
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5ConclusionAcross 36 months of post-pandemic surveillance in Tianjin (2,597 confirmed cases), HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading viral causes of pediatric LRTI, and each of the six viruses carried a distinctive age, sex, seasonal and specimen-type profile. In a unified model adjusting simultaneously for seasonality and secular trend, RSV and HMPV, rather than IFV, showed the clearest evidence of an independent, non-seasonal climate association, whereas IFV’s prominent unadjusted climate signal proved to reflect its strong intrinsic seasonality. HBoV showed a singular July epidemic at odds with the December convergence of the other viruses, together providing a preliminary basis for pathogen-tailored early warning and prevention in northern Chinese megacities. Co-infection occurred in 4.5% of positives, centered on HRV-containing combinations whose clinical severity remains to be defined. Set alongside pre-pandemic Chinese pediatric surveillance, these findings are broadly consistent with a post-pandemic pattern of intensified, temporally compressed winter transmission, while HBoV’s summer epidemic appears to be a locally distinctive feature warranting further study. If confirmed with higher-resolution, denominator-based data, these findings could inform a hospital-level operational calendar anchored on the December peak and the secondary July HBoV peak, climate-informed early warning tailored to each pathogen’s actual (seasonally adjusted) climate sensitivity, and a refined strategy for vaccination, RSV passive immunization and infection control. Such confirmation will require multi-center cohorts, denominator-based positivity metrics, weekly- or daily-resolution meteorology, and direct pre- versus post-pandemic comparison.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionLower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs)—comprising pneumonia, bronchiolitis, and related lower-airway syndromes—remain leading causes of pediatric hospitalization and mortality in children under five worldwide, with viruses accounting for the overwhelming majority of cases (Nair et al., 2010; Mulholland, 2003; Li et al., 2022). In contrast to generally self-limiting upper respiratory infections, viral LRTIs account disproportionately for admissions requiring supplemental oxygen and intensive care; moreover, certain pathogens, notably RSV and HRV, are implicated in long-term sequelae including recurrent wheeze and asthma (Li et al., 2022; Bizot et al., 2021; Royston and Tapparel, 2016). In China, the burden is amplified by dense urban populations, overlapping pathogen circulation, and the high contact rates among school-aged children, all of which sustain substantial LRTI-related hospitalizations (Cui et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). Following the lifting of pandemic-era non-pharmaceutical interventions, several Chinese regions reported atypical, out-of-season resurgences of RSV, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and ADV (Del Riccio et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). These have been attributed both to an immunity gap accumulated during 2020–2022 and to the re-establishment of pre-pandemic transmission networks (Cohen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024). Despite this evolving landscape, most national surveillance efforts remain narrowly focused on classical pathogens (RSV, ADV, IFV) or aggregate all respiratory infections irrespective of anatomical site. Consequently, the post-pandemic, multi-pathogen epidemiology of viral LRTI specifically in children—particularly at the city level, where targeted surveillance is most actionable—remains inadequately characterized (Terliesner et al., 2022; Xia et al., 2026).Ambient weather conditions are well-established modulators of respiratory virus transmission, operating through both physical and host-defense mechanisms (Baker et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2021). Cold, dry air favors the persistence and airborne dispersal of enveloped viruses such as RSV and influenza by stabilizing the lipid envelope, slowing droplet evaporation, and impairing upper-airway mucociliary clearance (Kudo et al., 2019; Lowen et al., 2007; Lowen and Steel, 2014). Non-enveloped viruses, including ADV and HBoV, whose protein capsids tolerate a wider range of environmental stressors, tend to circulate more evenly throughout the year (Chen et al., 2014b; Lion, 2014). Importantly, climate–virus relationships are non-linear and time-delayed; exposures occurring days to weeks before case surges often exert the dominant effect, a structure that makes distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) particularly suitable for fine-grained inference (Bhaskaran et al., 2013; Gasparrini et al., 2010; Gasparrini, 2011). A recent post-pandemic study from Wuhan, in central China, applied daily-resolution DLNMs to seven respiratory pathogens and identified distinct lagged climate patterns—most notably, humidity drops as 1–2-week antecedents of RSV surges and wind speed as a leading correlate of influenza activity (Li et al., 2025). Because only monthly-resolution meteorological data were available for the present 2023–2025 window (Section 2.3), a full DLNM cross-basis was not identifiable with the available degrees of freedom; we therefore adapted the same distributed-lag logic into a screening framework of single-lag quasi-Poisson models spanning 0–6-month lags, cross-validated against cross-correlation functions and, in a second step, adjusted for seasonality and secular trend within a unified model (Section 2.4). This approach is best viewed as a monthly-resolution approximation to the DLNM framework rather than a full non-linear cross-basis estimation.However, few studies have systematically examined this multi-pathogen landscape in northern China, where the continental monsoon climate—characterized by cold, dry winters; hot, humid summers; and pronounced seasonal swings in temperature, humidity, and wind—differs markedly from the subtropical conditions of Wuhan and other southern cities (Chen et al., 2014a; Cui et al., 2015; Yin et al., 2023). Tianjin, a megacity of 13 million on the North China Plain, offers a particularly valuable setting to address this gap. Its local viral spectrum extends beyond the four classical agents to include three pathogens that are less consistently surveilled but contribute substantially to pediatric LRTI: HRV, HBoV, and HMPV (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2020). Prior work in this area has concentrated largely on southern China or on the classical pathogens (RSV, ADV, IFV), and the lagged climatic effects of the less consistently surveilled HRV, HBoV and HMPV under a temperate continental climate have not been systematically evaluated. Precisely how these three viruses, alongside the classical agents, track climatic exposures across different lag intervals in northern China therefore remains poorly characterized—a knowledge gap that has direct implications for the design of climate-informed early-warning systems in the region.To address this, we analyzed three years of post-pandemic surveillance data (January 2023 to December 2025) from a tertiary children’s hospital in Tianjin, encompassing 2,597 virologically confirmed pediatric LRTI cases caused by six respiratory viruses. Our objectives were: (i) to describe the demographic, temporal, and specimen-type distributions of each pathogen; (ii) to characterize co-infection patterns; (iii) to test pathogen-specific associations with monthly meteorological variables using Spearman correlation and season-stratified analyses; and (iv) to evaluate lagged climate effects across 0- to 6-month intervals using cross-correlation functions and a unified quasi-Poisson generalized linear model that simultaneously adjusts for seasonality and secular trends. Finally, we discuss the practical implications of our findings for climate-informed early-warning systems and pathogen-tailored preventive strategies in northern Chinese megacities. 2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. It is generated by an integrated scoring system that combines normalized read counts (reads per million, RPM), the breadth of genome coverage achieved across the targeted regions, and spec…
