elements_en.study_design_and_population: HRV was the most frequently detected virus (796 cases, 30.7%), followed by ADV (692, 26.6%), RSV (536, 20.6%), HBoV (313, 12.1%), IFV (155, 6.0%) and HMPV (105, 4.0%) (Figure 2A; Table 1).
elements_en.methods: Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%).
elements_en.main_results: RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: To our knowledge, the dataset is unusual for northern China in spanning six respiratory viruses, including the comparatively under-surveyed HRV, HBoV and HMPV, over the full 2023–2025 post-pandemic rebound window, with a complete and time-matched monthly meteorological record.4.1Principal epidemiological featuresAcross the six viruses, HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading causes of pediatric LRTI, and each pathogen carried a well-defined demographic profile.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The strong age-group × pathogen association reinforces the need for an explicitly age-stratified surveillance framework.The six pathogens also fell into two distinct seasonal groups.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Co-infection occurred in 4.5% of positives, centered on HRV-containing combinations whose clinical severity remains to be defined.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: (C) 按病原体分组的年度病例负担。分组条形图和堆叠条形图面板显示(A)六种病原体的病例数和百分比,(B)按病原体分组的样本构成,以及(C)2023年至2025年的年度病例负担。
elements_zh.methods: 使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露因素。结果在2,597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统的发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023)一致;而HMPV则表现出中间分布。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据我们所知,该数据集在北方中国较为独特,因为它涵盖了2023年至2025年疫情后反弹期间的六种呼吸道病毒,包括相对较少被调查的HRV、HBoV和HMPV,并且拥有完整且时间匹配的每月气象记录。4.1主要流行病学特征在六种病毒中,HRV、ADV和RSV是导致儿童LRTI的主要原因,每种病原体都有明确的流行病学特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 强年龄组×病原体关联进一步强调了需要建立明确的年龄分层监测框架。这六种病原体也分为两个不同的季节性群体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 4.5%的阳性病例出现了合并感染,主要集中在包含HRV的组合中,其临床严重程度仍需进一步定义。

papers.title_zh: 流行病学和滞后气候驱动因素对中国天津市儿童病毒性下呼吸道感染(2023–2025)的影响
papers.source_body_en: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting and populationWe conducted a retrospective single-center surveillance study at the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Tianjin Children’s Hospital (Ma-Chang campus), the only tertiary-A comprehensive children’s hospital in Tianjin. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%),...
papers.abstract_zh: 背景在解除疫情管控措施后,中国经历了儿童呼吸道感染的急剧回升;然而,关于北方中国温带大陆性气候地区疫情后下呼吸道感染(LRTIs)的流行病学和气候数据仍然稀缺。方法本项回顾性单中心监测研究旨在描述天津住院儿童中六种呼吸道病毒在疫情后的流行病学情况,并评估其与气候因素的特定病原体相关性。2材料与方法2.1研究设计、设置和人群我们在天津儿童医院(马场校区)呼吸科开展回顾性单中心监测研究,该医院是天津唯一的三级甲等综合性儿童医院。这一标准适用于儿童而非实验室结果:每当tNGS报告中检测到细菌、非典型或非检测面板病毒病原体的同时也检测到六种目标病毒之一时,该病例将在资格筛选时被排除在队列研究之外,因此此处报告的任何分析均不包含此类儿童。2023年1月至2025年12月期间住院的0至18岁儿童接受了针对人类鼻病毒(HRV)、腺病毒(ADV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、人类博卡病毒(HBoV)、流感病毒(IFV)和人类副流感病毒(HMPV)的靶向下一代测序检测。使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露。结果在2597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)(图2A;表1)。

papers.title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and policy
papers.abstract: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on vaccination strategies for girls and women across the life course, with an emphasis on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its related entities. The central question is how to integrate vaccination into routine women's healthcare to prevent RSV-related diseases and improve health outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence-based recommendations from WHO, SAGE, CDC, ACOG, and national immunization technical advisory groups. It includes vaccines such as RSV, Tdap, influenza, hepatitis B, and others. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that vaccination across the life course is essential for preventing RSV-related diseases, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. It emphasizes the importance of maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integrating regular and opportunistic vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while RSV is a significant concern, vaccine-preventable diseases such as HPV-related cancers, influenza, and pertussis continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the effectiveness of RSV vaccines in specific populations and life stages, highlighting a gap in evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends practical implementation strategies and policy actions to support FIGO member societies in promoting equitable vaccination across the life course. It highlights the need for strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's healthcare to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity.

analysis.summary_en: This review emphasizes the importance of vaccination across the life course for girls and women, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other vaccine-preventable diseases. It highlights the role of healthcare providers in integrating vaccines into routine care and reducing health disparities. The review synthesizes recommendations from WHO, SAGE, CDC, and ACOG, focusing on maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and opportunistic vaccination. Despite the significance of RSV-related diseases, the review identifies gaps in evidence regarding vaccine effectiveness in specific populations and life stages. It calls for strengthened vaccine advocacy and policy actions to improve global health equity for girls and women.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种策略,特别强调呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)及其相关实体。核心问题是:如何将疫苗接种整合到常规女性健康护理中,以预防RSV相关疾病并改善健康结果。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述综合了来自世界卫生组织(WHO)、免疫接种战略咨询专家组(SAGE)、疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)、美国妇产科医师学会(ACOG)以及国家免疫技术咨询小组的循证建议。包括RSV、Tdap、流感、乙型肝炎等疫苗。综述未明确报告数据库、搜索日期或纳入标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种对于预防RSV相关疾病至关重要,尤其是在低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)以及移民人群中。它强调了母体疫苗接种、宫颈癌预防以及将常规和机会性疫苗接种整合到常规产科和妇科服务中的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管RSV是一个重要问题,但疫苗可预防的疾病,如与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的癌症、流感和百日咳,仍对女孩和女性造成不成比例的负担。缺乏关于RSV 疫苗在特定人群和生命阶段效果的全面数据,凸显了证据方面的空白。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议采取实际的实施策略和政策行动,以支持国际妇产科联盟(FIGO)成员协会在全生命周期内推动公平的疫苗接种。它强调了在女性健康护理中加强疫苗倡导的必要性,以减少可预防的发病率和死亡率,并促进健康公平。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种策略,特别强调呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)及其相关实体。核心问题是:如何将疫苗接种整合到常规女性健康护理中,以预防RSV相关疾病并改善健康结果。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述综合了来自世界卫生组织(WHO)、免疫接种战略咨询专家组(SAGE)、疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)、美国妇产科医师学会(ACOG)以及国家免疫技术咨询小组的循证建议。包括RSV、Tdap、流感、乙型肝炎等疫苗。综述未明确报告数据库、搜索日期或纳入标准。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,针对女孩和女性全生命周期的疫苗接种对于预防RSV相关疾病至关重要,尤其是在低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)以及移民人群中。它强调了母体疫苗接种、宫颈癌预防以及将常规和机会性疫苗接种整合到常规产科和妇科服务中的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管RSV是一个重要问题,但疫苗可预防的疾病,如与人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)相关的癌症、流感和百日咳,仍对女孩和女性造成不成比例的负担。缺乏关于RSV 疫苗在特定人群和生命阶段效果的全面数据,凸显了证据方面的空白。

papers.title: Appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms: A retrospective observational study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV place considerable pressure on healthcare systems. Inconsistent respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms may delay recognition of respiratory viral infections and implementation of appropriate infection prevention and control measures. OBJECTIVE: To assess the appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms and to identify factors associated with inappropriate screening. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study in a 2500-bed tertiary hospital in Belgium during three periods of the 2022-2023 influenza epidemic. Medical records were reviewed for demographic and clinical characteristics, respiratory symptoms, and respiratory virus screening practices. Screening was classified as appropriate or inappropriate (delayed or absent despite indication) based on prevailing guidelines. Determinants of inappropriate screening were explored using univariable analyses. RESULTS: Of 743 hospital admissions assessed for eligibility, 345 (46%) involved patients with respiratory symptoms and constituted the primary analysis population. Respiratory virus screening was appropriate in 75% (258/345) and inappropriate in 25% (87/345) of cases. Appropriate screening was more frequent among patients admitted for respiratory conditions and among those meeting criteria for severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). Screening appropriateness was significantly lower among patients who developed respiratory symptoms during hospitalization than among those with symptoms documented at admission (37% vs. Isolation status could not be reliably determined for 44% of patients and was therefore considered descriptive only. CONCLUSION: Gaps remain in appropriate respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms, particularly among patients who develop symptoms during hospitalization. Systematic symptom-based screening and standardized decision-support tools may help improve adherence to respiratory virus screening recommendations.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:SARS-CoV-2、流感病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等呼吸道病毒对医疗系统造成显著压力。对于有呼吸道症状的住院患者,不一致的呼吸道病毒筛查可能会延迟对呼吸道病毒感染的识别以及实施适当的感染预防和控制措施。目的:评估住院患者中呼吸道病毒筛查的适宜性,并确定与不适宜筛查相关的因素。方法:我们在比利时一家拥有2500张床位的三级医院,在2022-2023年流感流行期间的三个时期内开展了一项回顾性观察研究。审查了医疗记录,包括人口统计学和临床特征、呼吸道症状以及呼吸道病毒筛查实践。根据现行指南,将筛查分为适宜或不适宜(尽管有指征但延迟或缺失)。使用单变量分析探讨了不适宜筛查的决定因素。结果:在743例符合条件的住院病例中,有345例(46%)涉及有呼吸道症状的患者,构成了主要分析人群。在这些病例中,适宜的呼吸道病毒筛查占75%(258/345),而不适宜的筛查占25%(87/345)。对于因呼吸道疾病入院的患者以及符合严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)标准的患者,适宜的筛查更为常见。在住院期间出现呼吸道症状的患者中,筛查适宜性显著低于入院时已有症状的患者(37% vs. 未确定隔离状态的患者占44%,因此仅作为描述性分析。结论:对于有呼吸道症状的住院患者,呼吸道病毒筛查的适宜性仍存在差距,尤其是在住院期间出现症状的患者中。基于症状的系统性筛查和标准化的决策支持工具可能有助于提高对呼吸道病毒筛查建议的依从性。

papers.title: Salmeterol Attenuates RSV-Induced Inflammatory Responses in THP-1 Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a highly prevalent respiratory virus in children, and there is no effective antiviral drug therapy or vaccine available for the infant population. Monocytes are pivotal cells that produce cytokines that influence the inflammatory response. Since monocyte responses can be regulated by β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR) agonists, the aim of this study was to examine the effect of salmeterol, a long-acting β2-adrenergic (LABA) agonist, on the activation of monocytes during RSV infection. Here, we evaluated the effects of increasing concentrations of salmeterol (1 or 10 μM) on THP-1 cell viability, viral replication, and cellular responses, including nitric oxide, TNF-α and IL-1β production, as well as p38 MAPK pathway activation by Western blot analysis following RSV infection. Results revealed that salmeterol treatment was not cytotoxic and effectively reduced RSV-induced NO production, although it had no effect on RSV replication. Additional experiments demonstrated that salmeterol could downregulate the proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β in RSV-infected THP-1 monocytes. Furthermore, these effects appeared to be related to the downregulation of phosphorylated p38 MAPK, which was significantly increased during RSV infection. Overall, these findings suggest that salmeterol could be considered an anti-inflammatory adjuvant in RSV-induced inflammatory responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是一种在儿童中高度流行的呼吸道病毒,目前尚无有效的抗病毒药物或治疗手段可供婴儿使用。本研究旨在探讨长效β2-肾上腺素受体激动剂沙美特罗对RSV感染期间单核细胞激活的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究通过Western blot分析评估了不同浓度的沙美特罗(1或10 μM)对THP-1细胞存活率、病毒复制以及细胞反应的影响,包括一氧化氮(NO)、TNF-α和IL-1β的产生,以及p38 MAPK通路的激活情况。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用THP-1细胞评估沙美特罗对RSV诱导炎症反应的影响,包括通过Western blot分析评估一氧化氮(NO)、TNF-α和IL-1β的产生以及p38 MAPK通路的激活情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,沙美特罗并未表现出细胞毒性,并有效减少了RSV诱导的NO产生,但对RSV复制没有影响。进一步的实验表明,沙美特罗能够下调RSV感染的THP-1单核细胞中促炎细胞因子TNF-α和IL-1β的表达。此外,这些效应似乎与磷酸化p38 MAPK的下调有关,而磷酸化p38 MAPK在RSV感染期间显著增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,这些发现表明沙美特罗可被视为RSV诱导炎症反应中的抗炎辅助药物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为开发抗炎策略以管理婴儿中RSV诱导的炎症反应提供依据,可能补充现有的治疗手段。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是在体外使用THP-1细胞进行的,可能无法完全代表人类单核细胞的反应。证据强度中等,因为它基于体外实验,未包括体内数据。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为开发抗炎策略以管理婴儿中RSV诱导的炎症反应提供依据,可能补充现有的治疗手段。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是在体外使用THP-1细胞进行的,可能无法完全代表人类单核细胞的反应。证据强度中等,因为它基于体外实验,未包括体内数据。

papers.title: Prevalence of herpesvirus, polyomavirus, and respiratory viruses in saliva from a Quilombola community in the Brazilian Amazon
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Quilombola communities, composed of descendants of enslaved individuals from Brazil’s colonial period, often face limited access to healthcare, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections. Oral transmission routes, particularly through saliva, are relevant for viruses such as those in the Polyomaviridae family. Therefore, here we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HSV-1, JC (JCV), and BK polyomaviruses, and respiratory viruses (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2), as well as the salivary inflammatory profile in individuals from a Quilombola community. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 100 individuals. Oral health was assessed, and nucleic acids were analyzed using real-time PCR (JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1) and multiplex TaqMan PCR (RSV, Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2). Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified. Results BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01). SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles. No association was found between viral detection and tooth loss or the use of prosthesis. Conclusion A high prevalence of BKPyV and a salivary pro-inflammatory response were observed, highlighting potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil, involving 100 individuals.
analysis.methods: Unstimulated saliva samples were collected and analyzed using real-time PCR for JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1, and multiplex TaqMan PCR for RSV, Influenza A/B, and SARS-CoV-2. Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified.
analysis.main_results: BKPyV was detected in 19% of the samples, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01), and SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The high prevalence of BKPyV and the salivary pro-inflammatory response observed highlight potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that oral health surveillance and interventions may be necessary to address the increased risk of viral infections in Quilombola communities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not establish causality. The sample size of 100 individuals may also limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of herpesvirus, polyomavirus, and respiratory viruses in saliva from a Quilombola community in the Brazilian Amazon. BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. The findings highlight potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.

papers.title_zh: 巴西亚马逊地区奎隆博拉社区唾液中疱疹病毒、多瘤病毒和呼吸道病毒的检测情况
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Quilombola communities, composed of descendants of enslaved individuals from Brazil’s colonial period, often face limited access to healthcare, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections. Oral transmission routes, particularly through saliva, are relevant for viruses such as those in the Polyomaviridae family. Therefore, here we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HSV-1, JC (JCV), and BK polyomaviruses, and respiratory viruses (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2), as well as the salivary inflammatory profile in individuals from a Quilombola community. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 100 individuals. Oral health was assessed, and nucleic acids were analyzed using real-time PCR (JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1) and multiplex TaqMan PCR (RSV, Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2). Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified. Results BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ ( p < 0.01). SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles. No association was found between viral detection and tooth loss or the use of prosthesis. Conclusion A high prevalence of BKPyV and a salivary pro-inflammatory response were observed, highlighting potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 引言 奎隆博拉社区由巴西殖民时期奴隶的后裔组成,往往面临医疗资源获取受限的问题,这可能增加其对病毒感染的易感性。通过唾液传播的口腔传播途径,特别是多瘤病毒科的病毒,具有重要意义。因此,本研究旨在调查巴西亚马逊地区奎隆博拉社区个体唾液中HSV-1、JC(JCV)和BK多瘤病毒以及呼吸道病毒(流感A/B型、RSV、SARS-CoV-2)的检测情况,以及唾液中的炎症特征。方法 本研究在巴西帕拉州的奎隆博拉社区Mangabeira进行横断面研究,收集了100名个体的未刺激唾液样本。评估了口腔健康状况,并使用实时PCR(JCPyV、BKPyV、HSV-1)和多重TaqMan PCR(RSV、流感A/B型、SARS-CoV-2)分析了核酸。量化了细胞因子(IL-6、IFN-γ、TNF-α、IL-10)。结果 BKPyV在19%的样本中被检测到,而HSV-1和SARS-CoV-2各在3%的样本中被发现。未检测到JCPyV、RSV或流感病例。BKPyV感染与IFN-γ水平升高(p < 0.01)相关,SARS-CoV-2和HSV-1感染则与促炎细胞因子谱相关。未发现病毒检测与牙齿脱落或假牙使用之间存在关联。结论 观察到BKPyV的高检测率和唾液中的促炎反应,突显了这一被忽视群体可能存在的口腔健康脆弱性。

papers.title: Safety of nirsevimab in children aged 0–24 months: Analysis based on EudraVigilance data (2023–2025)
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, and it is associated with substantial morbidity, including hospitalization and death. After European Medicine Agency approval of nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody against RSV, immunization campaigns have been implemented in several European Union countries for administration to children as preventive intervention against severe RSV disease during RSV epidemic season. Monitoring its safety in routine healthcare practice is also important. We described suspected adverse drug reactions (ADRs) following nirsevimab administration in children aged 0-24 months, reported in the EudraVigilance system between 2023 and 2025. There were 1,923 ADRs, corresponding to 808 cases. By System Organ Class, ADRs mainly included general disorders and administration site conditions, which include nonspecific systemic manifestations and administration-site reactions that cannot be readily assigned to a single organ system (28.4%), infections and infestations (23.3%), respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (12.2%); by Preferred Terms most frequent were drug ineffective (12.6%), and RSV bronchiolitis (9.6%). In addition, pyrexia, rash, and injection site reactions were also common. This study offered systematic characterization of ADRs following administration of nirsevimab. It found that the reported ADRs are consistent with the safety results from pre- and real-world safety studies. Our study can support the continue monitoring of the real-world safety and guide the planning of analytical observational studies on the safety profile of nirsevimab.

Our study can support the continue monitoring of the real-world safety and guide the planning of analytical observational studies on the safety profile of nirsevimab.

papers.title: Nirsevimab reduced acute otitis media infections in infants—a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections in young children worldwide. Acute otitis media (AOM) is among the most frequent complications of RSV infection and the leading indication for antibiotic prescribing in this age group. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of nirsevimab in reducing the incidence of AOM among infants. We conducted a nationwide register-based interrupted time-series study using data on live births, laboratory-confirmed RSV detections, and AOM diagnoses from four consecutive RSV seasons (2022-2023 to 2025-2026). Monthly infant populations at risk were reconstructed from birth cohorts to estimate incidence rates during the peak RSV seasons (December-March) which were compared between two pre-implementation and two post-implementation RSV seasons in infants aged < 12 months, stratified into age groups of 0-2, 3-5, and 6-11 months. The study population consisted of 181,999 infants and the follow-up consisted of 2,022,261 infant-months. A total of 3699 RSV-positive findings and 15,830 AOM diagnoses were included in the primary analysis. Following nirsevimab implementation, the incidence of AOM and RSV among infants aged < 12 months decreased by 44% (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.54-0.58) and 83% (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.15-0.18), respectively. The reduction was greatest in the youngest age (0-2 months) group. CONCLUSION: Implementation of a nirsevimab immunisation programme was associated with a substantial reduction in AOM incidence among infants aged < 12 months, suggesting that RSV immunisation may reduce the burden of AOM in early childhood. WHAT'S KNOWN: • RSV is a major cause of morbidity during infancy, and acute otitis media is among its most frequent complications. • Nirsevimab has demonstrated high efficacy in preventing severe RSV disease in young children; however, its effect on outpatient RSV-related complications has not been well established. WHAT IS NEW: • This study provides population-based real-world evidence on the impact of nirsevimab on acute otitis media. • Following the implementation of nirsevimab prophylaxis, the incidence of acute otitis media among infants decreased significantly.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用了四次连续呼吸道合胞病毒季节(2022-2023至2025-2026)的出生数据、实验室确认的呼吸道合胞病毒检测数据和急性中耳炎诊断数据,开展了一项全国范围的基于登记的中断时间序列研究。研究人群包括181,999名婴儿,随访时间为2,022,261个婴儿月。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过从出生队列研究重建每月婴儿风险人群,以估算在呼吸道合胞病毒高发季节(12月至次年3月)的急性中耳炎发病率,并将其与两个实施前和两个实施后的呼吸道合胞病毒季节进行比较,比较对象为<12个月的婴儿,按年龄分为0-2个月、3-5个月和6-11个月三个组别。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 实施尼塞韦单抗疫苗接种计划与<12个月婴儿急性中耳炎发病率的显著下降相关,表明呼吸道合胞病毒疫苗可能有助于减轻婴幼儿早期的急性中耳炎负担。本研究提供了基于人群的现实世界证据,说明尼塞韦单抗疫苗对急性中耳炎的影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,呼吸道合胞病毒疫苗可能有助于减轻婴幼儿早期的急性中耳炎负担,这可能为未来预防呼吸道合胞病毒相关并发症的公共卫生策略提供依据。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于登记数据,未包括详细的实验室或临床程序。证据是基于人群的现实世界证据,这为研究结果提供了中等程度的信心。

papers.title: Size, cytopathic effects, and prevalence of Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV in healthcare settings
papers.abstract: Airborne transmission of respiratory viruses in healthcare settings is difficult to assess, particularly with respect to the size and viability of virus-containing aerosols. Most field studies rely on molecular detection, which limits inference about the infectiousness of virus. In this study we collected size-resolved airborne samples in a dental clinic and hospital during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season using a BC (BioCascade)-BioSpot VIVAS (Viable Virus Aerosol Sampler). We analyzed these samples by RT-PCR and culture-based assays for influenza A, influenza B, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Viral RNA was detected in 11.1% of the 81 sampling events, with the highest positivity (25%) observed in pulmonary unit patient rooms. When influenza and SARS-CoV-2 RNA were detected, all of these detections occurred in the 4-10 μm size fraction, whereas all RSV RNA was detected in the <1.5 μm size fraction. Cell culture assays confirmed the presence of viable influenza in the samples that were positive by RT-PCR. Plaques were only observed for influenza A viral positive samples at the ‘neat’ or undiluted rate, whereas RSV and SARS-CoV-2 did not produce cytopathic effects in the cell culture assays. These findings highlight virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable virus from field-collected bioaerosols in healthcare environments.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess airborne transmission of respiratory viruses in healthcare settings, focusing on the size and viability of virus-containing aerosols, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study collected size-resolved airborne samples in a dental clinic and hospital during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season, with 81 sampling events conducted across different locations.
analysis.methods: Airborne samples were collected using a BC-BioSpot VIVAS (Viable Virus Aerosol Sampler) and analyzed by RT-PCR and culture-based assays for influenza A, influenza B, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.main_results: Viral RNA was detected in 11.1% of the 81 sampling events, with the highest positivity (25%) observed in pulmonary unit patient rooms. All RSV RNA was detected in the <1.5 μm size fraction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable virus from field-collected bioaerosols in healthcare environments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform the development of targeted surveillance and control strategies for RSV in healthcare settings, particularly regarding aerosol size and viability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on molecular detection rather than direct infectiousness assessment, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated airborne transmission of respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), in healthcare settings during the 2024-2025 season. Using a BC-BioSpot VIVAS sampler, size-resolved airborne samples were collected in a dental clinic and hospital. RT-PCR and culture-based assays identified viral RNA in 11.1% of sampling events, with RSV RNA predominantly detected in the <1.5 μm size fraction. The results emphasize virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable RSV from field samples. While the findings contribute to understanding RSV transmission dynamics, the study relies on molecular detection rather than direct infectiousness assessment, limiting the strength of the evidence. These results may inform targeted surveillance and control strategies for RSV in healthcare environments.

papers.title_zh: 流感、SARS-CoV-2和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)在医疗保健环境中气溶胶的大小、细胞病变效应和患病率
papers.source_body_en: Airborne transmission of respiratory viruses in healthcare settings is difficult to assess, particularly with respect to the size and viability of virus-containing aerosols. Most field studies rely on molecular detection, which limits inference about the infectiousness of virus. In this study we collected size-resolved airborne samples in a dental clinic and hospital during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season using a BC (BioCascade)-BioSpot VIVAS (Viable Virus Aerosol Sampler). We analyzed these samples by RT-PCR and culture-based assays for influenza A, influenza B, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Viral RNA was detected in 11.1% of the 81 sampling events, with the highest positivity (25%) observed in pulmonary unit patient rooms. When influenza and SARS-CoV-2 RNA were detected, all of these detections occurred in the 4-10 μm size fraction, whereas all RSV RNA was detected in the <1.5 μm size fraction. Cell culture assays confirmed the presence of viable influenza in the samples that were positive by RT-PCR. Plaques were only observed for influenza A viral positive samples at the ‘neat’ or undiluted rate, whereas RSV and SARS-CoV-2 did not produce cytopathic effects in the cell culture assays. These findings highlight virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable virus from field-collected bioaerosols in healthcare environments.
papers.abstract_zh: 在医疗保健环境中评估呼吸道病毒气溶胶的传播性(传播)具有挑战性,尤其是在病毒气溶胶的大小和活性方面。大多数现场研究依赖于分子检测,这限制了对病毒传染性的推断。本研究在2024-2025年呼吸道病毒季节期间,使用BC(BioCascade)-BioSpot VIVAS(可培养病毒气溶胶采样器)在牙科诊所和医院中收集了具有粒径分辨率的空气样本。我们通过RT-PCR和基于培养的检测方法分析了这些样本,以检测流感A型、流感B型、SARS-CoV-2和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)。在81次采样事件中,有11.1%的样本检测到病毒RNA,其中肺病单元病房的阳性率最高(25%)。当检测到流感和SARS-CoV-2的RNA时,所有检测均发生在4-10 μm粒径组分中,而所有RSV RNA均检测到在<1.5 μm粒径组分中。细胞培养检测证实了通过RT-PCR检测为阳性的样本中存在可培养的流感病毒。仅在流感A型病毒阳性样本中观察到斑块,而RSV和SARS-CoV-2在细胞培养检测中未产生细胞病变效应。这些发现突显了不同病毒在气溶胶粒径分布上的特异性差异,以及在医疗保健环境中从现场收集的生物气溶胶中回收活性病毒的挑战。

papers.title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0–14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022–2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

analysis.methods: The study utilized the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database for analysis, including deaths and DALYs for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0–14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country.
analysis.main_results: In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with a decline in mortality and DALY rates by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The burden was highest in infants aged <1 year, and India had the highest burden, while Australia had the lowest.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members, with the burden inversely correlated with Sociodemographic Index.

papers.title: Pathogen spectrum and triple-criteria interpretation algorithm of BALF-targeted NGS in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan: a single-center retrospective study
papers.abstract: Background Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) causes substantial pediatric hospitalization and respiratory failure in mountainous western China. Conventional microbial assays show limited sensitivity for fastidious pathogens and mixed infections. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) using bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) enables broad-spectrum pathogen detection at lower cost than whole-metagenomic sequencing. However, many previous tNGS studies directly equate multiple microbial nucleic-acid signals with true coinfection, which may lead to unnecessary combined anti-infective therapy. Methods This single-center retrospective study enrolled 86 children aged 1.0 × 10 6 copies/mL), inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT), and chest imaging to discriminate genuine active coinfection from airway colonization. This load threshold was empirical and not internally validated by ROC analysis in our dataset. Patients were stratified into four age subgroups; diagnostic concordance was assessed among 34 patients with parallel routine microbial tests. Results In total, 229 pathogen isolates were identified. Viruses predominated (58.9%, 135/229), followed by bacteria (32.8%, 75/229). The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae (32.56%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (30.23%), and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A, 18.60%). While 82.6% (71/86) of patients harbored ≥2 pathogen nucleic-acid signals, only 17.4% (15/86) fulfilled criteria for clinical coinfection, dominated by virus-bacterial dual infection. Viral detection rates tended to decline with increasing age, whereas bacterial positivity was higher among preschool- and school-age children. A prominent spring epidemic peak was observed during May-June 2023. Only 22.86% of paired routine microbial tests showed full concordance with tNGS. These single-center data cannot be generalized to all pediatric severe-pneumonia populations. Most abundant multi-pathogen tNGS signals represented colonization or residual dead-microbe nucleic acid instead of true active infection. Conclusion Our triple-criteria interpretive framework offers standardized rules for grassroots mountain hospitals to reduce over-prescription of combined antibiotics and antivirals when interpreting BALF-tNGS results for children with refractory SCAP.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the limitations of conventional microbial assays in detecting fastidious pathogens and mixed infections in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective study was conducted at a hospital in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan, enrolling 86 children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia between specific dates.
analysis.methods: Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) using bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was employed to detect pathogens, alongside clinical parameters such as viral load thresholds, inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT), and chest imaging to differentiate genuine active coinfection from airway colonization.
analysis.main_results: A total of 229 pathogen isolates were identified, with viruses predominating at 58.9% (135/229), followed by bacteria at 32.8% (75/229). The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae (32.56%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (30.23%), and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A, 18.60%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study introduced a triple-criteria interpretive framework to standardize the analysis of BALF-tNGS results, aiming to reduce the over-prescription of combined antibiotics and antivirals in clinical practice.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the pathogen spectrum in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia, highlighting the importance of distinguishing true coinfections from colonization to guide appropriate treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's single-center design limits its generalizability to broader pediatric severe-pneumonia populations, and the load threshold used was empirical without internal validation by ROC analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the pathogen spectrum and introduced a triple-criteria interpretation algorithm for bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF)-targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) in children with refractory severe community-acquired pneumonia in mountainous Northeastern Sichuan. The research aimed to address the limitations of conventional microbial assays, which often fail to detect fastidious pathogens and mixed infections accurately. Using tNGS, 229 pathogen isolates were identified, with viruses predominating at 58.9%, followed by bacteria at 32.8%. The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A). While 82.6% of patients had multiple pathogen signals, only 17.4% met the criteria for clinical coinfection. The study proposed a framework to standardize tNGS interpretation, reducing unnecessary combined anti-infective therapy. However, the single-center design limits generalizability, and the viral load threshold was empirical without internal validation. The findings suggest that tNGS can improve detection of pathogens in this specific pediatric population, but caution is needed in interpreting multi-pathogen signals as true infections.

papers.title_zh: 靶向BALF的NGS病原谱及三标准解释算法在川东北山区难治性重症社区获得性肺炎儿童中的应用:一项单中心回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Background Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) causes substantial pediatric hospitalization and respiratory failure in mountainous western China. Conventional microbial assays show limited sensitivity for fastidious pathogens and mixed infections. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) using bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) enables broad-spectrum pathogen detection at lower cost than whole-metagenomic sequencing. However, many previous tNGS studies directly equate multiple microbial nucleic-acid signals with true coinfection, which may lead to unnecessary combined anti-infective therapy. Methods This single-center retrospective study enrolled 86 children aged 1.0 × 10 6 copies/mL), inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT), and chest imaging to discriminate genuine active coinfection from airway colonization. This load threshold was empirical and not internally validated by ROC analysis in our dataset. Patients were stratified into four age subgroups; diagnostic concordance was assessed among 34 patients with parallel routine microbial tests. Results In total, 229 pathogen isolates were identified. Viruses predominated (58.9%, 135/229), followed by bacteria (32.8%, 75/229). The three most frequent pathogens were Haemophilus influenzae (32.56%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (30.23%), and respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV-A, 18.60%). While 82.6% (71/86) of patients harbored ≥2 pathogen nucleic-acid signals, only 17.4% (15/86) fulfilled criteria for clinical coinfection, dominated by virus-bacterial dual infection. Viral detection rates tended to decline with increasing age, whereas bacterial positivity was higher among preschool- and school-age children. A prominent spring epidemic peak was observed during May-June 2023. Only 22.86% of paired routine microbial tests showed full concordance with tNGS. These single-center data cannot be generalized to all pediatric severe-pneumonia populations. Most abundant multi-pathogen tNGS signals represented colonization or residual dead-microbe nucleic acid instead of true active infection. Conclusion Our triple-criteria interpretive framework offers standardized rules for grassroots mountain hospitals to reduce over-prescription of combined antibiotics and antivirals when interpreting BALF-tNGS results for children with refractory SCAP.

papers.title: Modern aspects of respiratory syncytial viral infection in children: etiology, epidemiology, immunopathogenesis (scientific review, part 1)
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus is the leading etiological factor in respiratory diseases in children worldwide, the main cause of more than 30 million annual lower respiratory tract infections, as well as more than 3 million hospitalizations and 100,000 deaths annually among children under 5 years of age. At the same time, infants in the first six months of life, including premature infants, who are characterized by a severe course of infection with damage to the lower respiratory tract, a high percentage of hospitalization, including in the intensive care unit, are especially vulnerable. The mortality rate of young children from respiratory syncytial infection is 3.6%. The aim of the study was to analyze the current literature on the structure of respiratory syncytial virus, its pathogenicity and virulence, and factors that contribute to the escape from the innate immune system. To study the epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infection during the COVID-19 pandemic and the postpandemic period, as well as the pathogenesis of the infectious process and pathomorphological changes in organs and systems.

source_records.title: Modern aspects of respiratory syncytial viral infection in children: etiology, epidemiology, immunopathogenesis (scientific review, part 1)
source_records.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus is the leading etiological factor in respiratory diseases in children worldwide, the main cause of more than 30 million annual lower respiratory tract infections, as well as more than 3 million hospitalizations and 100,000 deaths annually among children under 5 years of age. At the same time, infants in the first six months of life, including premature infants, who are characterized by a severe course of infection with damage to the lower respiratory tract, a high percentage of hospitalization, including in the intensive care unit, are especially vulnerable. The mortality rate of young children from respiratory syncytial infection is 3.6%. The aim of the study was to analyze the current literature on the structure of respiratory syncytial virus, its pathogenicity and virulence, and factors that contribute to the escape from the innate immune system. To study the epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infection during the COVID-19 pandemic and the postpandemic period, as well as the pathogenesis of the infectious process and pathomorphological changes in organs and systems.

papers.title: Ensemble model-based prediction of school-age asthma risk in children with food allergy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention. OBJECTIVE: To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support. METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds. RESULTS: On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver. CONCLUSION: The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2. IMPACT: Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors. SIGNIFICANCE: Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop an ensemble-learning model for early asthma risk screening in infants with food allergy (0-2 years) using clinical data. The model incorporated 135 baseline predictors across seven categories and was trained on a prospective cohort of 447 FA-confirmed infants, with a median follow-up of 4.5 years. The results showed that the model achieved an AUC of 0.886 and recall of 1.00, with no missed cases in the independent test set. papers.title: Respiratory Pathogen Spectrum Among 12,220 Testing Episodes for Clinically Suspected Acute Respiratory Infection in Predominantly Hospitalized Patients at a Tertiary Hospital in Wuhan, China, 2025: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) impose a substantial global disease burden, yet the post-pandemic pathogen spectrum in central China remains incompletely characterized. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 12,220 consecutive testing episodes in which a 12-pathogen multiplex PCR panel was ordered for selected patients with clinically suspected ARI at Wuhan No. 1 Hospital in 2025; 99.7% occurred during hospitalization. Overall pathogen detection was 30.3% (3705/12,220). Human rhinovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (8.84%), followed by influenza A virus (5.29%), respiratory syncytial virus (4.75%), SARS-CoV-2 (4.13%), and human coronavirus (3.77%). Detection rates varied by age (children 60.4% vs. adults 23.3% and elderly 24.6%) and season (autumn 34.1%, winter 33.1%, spring 29.2%, summer 25.4%), with a monthly peak in November (39.3%) and trough in August (21.5%). Co-detection of two or more pathogens occurred in 343 positive episodes (9.26%), with HRV plus RSV being the most common pairing (12.8%). In multivariable analysis, clinical department (pediatrics aOR 5.84, 95% CI 3.69–9.49; hematology aOR 2.19, 95% CI 1.76–2.74) and season (autumn aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.39–1.77) were independently associated with pathogen detection, whereas sex was not. The strong pediatric age association (aOR 4.99, 95% CI 4.42–5.65) was attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for department (aOR 1.30, 95% CI 0.82–2.00), reflecting near-complete overlap between young age and pediatric attendance, which precludes separation of the two effects; within childhood, detection nevertheless decreased with increasing age (p for trend < 0.0001). These findings characterize pathogen detection among predominantly hospitalized patients with clinically suspected ARI at a single tertiary center and may inform local diagnostic stewardship and infection-control practice.

papers.title: Is Wastewater Surveillance Predictive during the Endemic Phase of Respiratory Disease? An Analysis Based on Clinical, Wastewater, and Digital Search Data in Detroit, Michigan
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the predictive value of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) during the endemic phase of respiratory diseases, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza A (IAV), influenza B (IBV), and SARS-CoV-2. The research evaluates how WBE data can provide early warnings and predictions for these diseases by comparing wastewater concentrations with clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. The study monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in Detroit’s wastewater from April 2020 to July 2025, and during the endemic phase, from October 2022 to March 2025, it also tracked RSV, IAV, and IBV. Methods included Pearson correlations, time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC), and random forest models to analyze the associations and temporal dynamics between wastewater data and clinical outcomes. The findings demonstrate that WBE can offer early insights into the endemic phase of respiratory diseases, supporting its use as a surveillance tool. However, the study does not report specific limitations of the methods or design, which may affect the confidence in the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity.
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了WBE在识别SARS-CoV-2疫情向地方性流行转变以及在后疫情时代对流感A(IAV)和B(IBV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和SARS-CoV-2等多种监测系统中提供早期预警的潜力。我们从2020年4月8日到2025年7月31日监测了底特律市废水中的SARS-CoV-2 N1浓度,生成了该市最早的、持续时间最长的废水数据集。
elements_zh.methods: 采用皮尔逊相关系数量化废水浓度与临床、综合征和数字流行病学数据之间的关联。时间滞后交叉相关(TLCC)用于分析这些数据集之间的时序动态,并确定每种疾病最早出现的数据和时间滞后。建立了随机森林模型,以基于WBE数据集预测临床病例。
elements_zh.main_results: 在流行期,从2022年10月1日到2025年3月31日,我们监测了底特律污水中的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、甲型流感病毒(IAV)、乙型流感病毒(IBV)和SARS-CoV-2。本研究展示了在流行期中废水基疾病监测(WBE)的预测价值,为季节性呼吸道疾病,包括新冠状病毒病(COVID-19)、流感和类似流感的疾病提供早期预警和预测。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这是首批使用基于废水的分析方法识别SARS-CoV-2疫情向地方性流行转变的研究之一。在这些呼吸道疾病的地方性流行阶段,系统分析了废水数据与传统临床、综合征和数字流行病学监测数据之间的关系。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为季节性呼吸道疾病(包括RSV 毛细支气管炎、RSV感染和流感)提供了早期预警和预测,展示了WBE作为公共卫生监测的潜在补充工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告研究设计或数据收集方法的具体局限性。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了WBE在识别SARS-CoV-2疫情向地方性流行转变以及在后疫情时代对流感A(IAV)和B(IBV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和SARS-CoV-2等多种监测系统中提供早期预警的潜力。我们从2020年4月8日到2025年7月31日监测了底特律市废水中的SARS-CoV-2 N1浓度,生成了该市最早的、持续时间最长的废水数据集。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用皮尔逊相关系数量化废水浓度与临床、综合征和数字流行病学数据之间的关联。时间滞后交叉相关(TLCC)用于分析这些数据集之间的时序动态,并确定每种疾病最早出现的数据和时间滞后。建立了随机森林模型,以基于WBE数据集预测临床病例。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在流行期,从2022年10月1日到2025年3月31日,我们监测了底特律污水中的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、甲型流感病毒(IAV)、乙型流感病毒(IBV)和SARS-CoV-2。本研究展示了在流行期中废水基疾病监测(WBE)的预测价值,为季节性呼吸道疾病,包括新冠状病毒病(COVID-19)、流感和类似流感的疾病提供早期预警和预测。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这是首批使用基于废水的分析方法识别SARS-CoV-2疫情向地方性流行转变的研究之一。在这些呼吸道疾病的地方性流行阶段,系统分析了废水数据与传统临床、综合征和数字流行病学监测数据之间的关系。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为季节性呼吸道疾病(包括RSV 毛细支气管炎、RSV感染和流感)提供了早期预警和预测,展示了WBE作为公共卫生监测的潜在补充工具。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告研究设计或数据收集方法的具体局限性。

papers.full_text: Safe and effective short-course intravenous antibiotic therapy in neonates under 28 days with urinary tract infection Mathilde Baudin Sorbonne University Jean-Daniel Delbet Sorbonne University Charlène Ferrandiz Sorbonne University Martin Auger Sorbonne University Gael Cals Sorbonne University Antoine Mouche Sorbonne University Mathie Lorrot Sorbonne University Tim Ulinski Sorbonne University Cyrielle Parmentier Sorbonne University Research Article Keywords: Posted Date: March 22nd, 2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8917425/v1 License:   This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. Read Full License Page 1/17 Additional Declarations: No competing interests reported. Version of Record: A version of this preprint was published at European Journal of Pediatrics on October 8th, 2026. See the published version at https://doi.org/10.1007/s00431-026-07412-5. Page 2/17 Abstract Aims Evidence guiding the optimal duration of intravenous (IV) antibiotic therapy for urinary tract infections (UTI) in neonates under 28 days remains scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of a short IV antibiotic course (≤ 4 days) in neonates with UTI. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-center study including neonates < 28 days hospitalized for culture- proven UTI (≥ 10,000 leukocytes/mL and ≥ 10,000 CFU/mL of a single pathogen). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were collected. Patients were stratified as low-risk (no severity criteria) or high-risk (clinical severity, bacteremia, pyelo-ureteral dilatation, or ESBL infection). The primary endpoint was 30-day recurrence after IV therapy. Results A total of 138 patients were included; (82% male, median age 15.5 days). 97 patients (71%) were classified as low-risk, and 95 of them (98%) received a short IV antibiotics (≤ 4 days). Only one early recurrence occurred related to poor oral intake of antibiotic treatment during viral co-infection. Escherichia coli was the predominant pathogen (88%). ESBL identified in 3.6% of neonates. Fifty-one patients (37%) were younger than 14 days, they presented less frequently with fever but received similar short IV courses without increased recurrence. Conclusion Short-course IV antibiotic therapy followed by oral treatment appears safe and effective for carefully selected neonates under 28 days with UTI and low risk factors for severe infection. These findings support a more tailored approach to antibiotic duration in this age group and call for prospective multicenter validation. What is Known Evidence supports short IV antibiotic courses in infants >28 days with UTI. Robust recommendations are lacking for neonates <28 days. What is New In clinically stable neonates <28 days without bacteremia, short IV therapy was not associated with increased recurrence. Even neonates ≤14 days can be safely managed with this approach. Page 3/17 Introduction Urinary tract infection (UTI) is the most frequent serious bacterial infection in neonates. Approximately 10–20% of febrile episodes in infants younger than 60 days are attributed to UTIs (1) (2), making them a leading cause of hospitalization in this age group. In the United States alone, over 20,000 children under the age of 1 year are hospitalized annually for UTIs (3). In UTIs of infants older than 28 days, intravenous (IV), antibiotics are not always required : oral and parenteral treatments have demonstrated comparable efficacy, and the parenteral phase is usually limited to less than 4 days. (4). According to guidelines, antibiotic selection should be tailored based on local antimicrobial resistance patterns. The 2024 French guidelines recommend initial hospitalization with intravenous therapy for infants < 3 months. No recommendations are provided regarding oral step- down therapy, and empirical oral antibiotics at diagnosis are not advised (5). Prolonged IV antibiotic therapy, is generally reserved for high risk situations (initial sepsis, uropathy, bacteremia), or UTI caused by an Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organism, when oral therapy is not feasible (6). In clinical practice, it is essential to determine the optimal time to switch from intravenous to oral antibiotic treatment. Insufficient treatment of UTIs increases the risk of recurrence, urosepsis (7), and long-term complications such as renal scarring. At this age, intravenous treatment cannot be administered on an outpatient basis and requires hospitalization. Shortening the duration of IV therapy offers several advantages: it reduces the risk of complication related to intravenous lines and medications -related adverse events (8); it limits disruption to parent-infant bonding (9), it decreases the length of hospital stay, thereby increasing bed availability and reducing healthcare costs (10). A recent systematic review (2022) concluded that shorter IV antibiotic courses (≤ 7 days in cases of bacteremia and < 4 days without bacteremia) are appropriate for managing urinary tract infections (UTIs) in infants under 3 months of age, without meningitis, or sepsis (11). For neonates younger than 28 days, evidence-based recommendations on the optimal duration of IV antibiotic therapy are lacking. Current European, American, and Asian guidelines provide no specific guidance for this age group (12–15). Although American studies report no increased 60-day recurrence risk with short IV courses (< 4 days) (7, 16), they included broader infant populations, leaving uncertainty for neonates < 28 days. Within this group, two aspects warrant attention: infants ≤ 14 days, who may present atypically, and the potential role of procalcitonin (PCT) as a severity marker(16). The present studyfocuses specifically on neonates under 28 days. Our objectives were to describe their clinical and microbiological characteristics and to assess whether criteria, established for older infants, can be safely applied to support short IV antibiotic course (< 4 days), without increasing the risk of early recurrence. Patients and Methods Page 4/17 Study design and Population We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the university Trousseau Hospital, between 2019 to 2023. Eligible participants were infants under 28 days of age who presented to the emergency department and were subsequently hospitalized with a diagnostic of UTI. UTI was defined as the presence of ≥ 10,000 leukocytes /mL in urinalysis and ≥ 10,000 CFUs/mL of a single pathogen in urine culture. Patients were identified using ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases) codes: N10 (acute tubulointerstitial nephritis) and N11 (chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis). We excluded preterm infants (< 35 weeks gestational age), meningitis or viral co-infections. Data Collection We collected demographic and clinical data included sex, age, weight, and the presence of risk factors for early neonatal bacterial UTIs. Clinical severity at presentation was assessed based on poor peripheral perfusion (skin recoloration time greater than 3 seconds, mottling, systolic blood pressure below 60 mmHg), need for fluid resuscitation, or admission to intensive care. Laboratory data was collected at the initial presentation to the emergency department and included blood culture results, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), total white blood cell count, neutrophil count, urine culture results, and bacterial identification. All patients underwent renal ultrasonography before the third day of treatment. Therapeutic data included antibiotic regimen details: route of administration, total length of hospital stay, and duration of fever following antibiotic initiation. Follow-up data encompassedprescription of antibiotic prophylaxis, voiding cystourethrography results, and vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) grading according to the International System of Radiographic Grading. Risk stratification and treatment duration Patients were stratified according to the risk of severe infection, based on international recommendations for infants aged 1–3 months (11–14), with additional safety criteria adapted for our neonatal population. These adaptations were implemented to ensure a conservative and standardized approach to treatment decisions. Low-risk group neonates with no risk factors for severe infection. High-risk group Page 5/17 neonates presenting with one or more of the following risk factors Clinical severity at presentation (poor perfusion, need for fluid resuscitation, or intensive care admission) Concurrent bacteremia Presence of pyelo-ureteral dilatation on renal imaging, considered a potential marker of underlying uropathy and added as a safety criterion in our protocol Infection caused by ESBL–producing organisms, limiting oral antibiotic options IV antibiotic duration was categorized as: Short course: ≤4 days of IV therapy Long course: >4 days of IV therapy All patients subsequently completed a total of 10-days antibiotic course, with oral therapy following the IV phase. Primary Endpoint The primary endpoint was a favorable infection course, defined as absence of UTI recurrence within 30 days of discharge. A 30 days window was chosen because most neonatal UTI recurrences occur within the first month, and this cut-off is used in previous pediatric studies (11). Recurrence was defined as readmission with culture-proven UTI with the same pathogen. Secondary Endpoints included: Secondary outcomes included (i) the clinical and biological description of neonates ≤ 14 days of age compared with older infants, and (ii) the association between elevated procalcitonin (PCT > 0.5 μg/L) and clinical or radiological features. Statistical analysis Descriptive statistics for quantitative variables were presented as median with interquartile range (IQR, 25th -75th percentiles), and qualitative variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. The normality of distribution for continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. For comparing dichotomous variables between groups, the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test was used as appropriate. For continuous variables with non-normal distribution, the Mann-Whitney U test was applied. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. All statistical analyses were performed using Sigma Plot. Results Page 6/17 Patient characteristics Of the 156 neonates initially identified, 138 were included in the final analysis. Eighteen neonates were excluded: 5 were born prematurely, 8 presented nosocomial UTI, and 5 presented UTI associated with meningitis (Fig. 1). The cohort comprised 113 boys (82%) with a median age of 15.5 days. Risk factor for neonatal infection were identified in 50 patients (36%). Clinical severity at presentation was observed in 4 patients (3%): they presented with signs of peripheral hypoperfusion and received fluid resuscitation; two of them were admitted to the intensive care unit, and one of these had bacteremia. Bacteremia was documented in 4 neonates (3%), and pyelo-ureteral dilatation (unilateral or bilateral) in 36 patients (26%). Fever was present in 97 patients (70%) with 23 (17%) febrile for more than 12 hours before admission. At the initial presentation to the emergency department, median CRP was 26 mg/L [IQR 4; 69] and median PCT was 0.38 μg/L [IQR 0.16; 1.97]. Imaging evidence of nephritis or pyelitis was present in 35 patients (25%) (Table 1). Only two low-risk patients received longer IV courses: one due to a significantly elevated PCT level of 32 μg/L, and one without clear explanation. Version of Record: A version of this preprint was published at European Journal of Pediatrics on October 8th, 2026. See the published version at https://doi.org/10.1007/s00431-026-07412-5. Page 2/17 Abstract Aims Evidence guiding the optimal duration of intravenous (IV) antibiotic therapy for urinary tract infections (UTI) in neonates under 28 days remains scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of a short IV antibiotic course (≤ 4 days) in neonates with UTI. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-center study including neonates < 28 days hospitalized for culture- proven UTI (≥ 10,000 leukocytes/mL and ≥ 10,000 CFU/mL of a single pathogen). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were collected. Patients were stratified as low-risk (no severity criteria) or high-risk (clinical severity, bacteremia, pyelo-ureteral dilatation, or ESBL infection). The primary endpoint was 30-day recurrence after IV therapy. Results A total of 138 patients were included; (82% male, median age 15.5 days). 97 patients (71%) were classified as low-risk, and 95 of them (98%) received a short IV antibiotics (≤ 4 days). Only one early recurrence occurred related to poor oral intake of antibiotic treatment during viral co-infection. Escherichia coli was the predominant pathogen (88%). ESBL identified in 3.6% of neonates. Fifty-one patients (37%) were younger than 14 days, they presented less frequently with fever but received similar short IV courses without increased recurrence. Conclusion Short-course IV antibiotic therapy followed by oral treatment appears safe and effective for carefully selected neonates under 28 days with UTI and low risk factors for severe infection. These findings support a more tailored approach to antibiotic duration in this age group and call for prospective multicenter validation. What is Known Evidence supports short IV antibiotic courses in infants >28 days with UTI. Robust recommendations are lacking for neonates <28 days. What is New In clinically stable neonates <28 days without bacteremia, short IV therapy was not associated with increased recurrence. Even neonates ≤14 days can be safely managed with this approach. Page 3/17 Introduction Urinary tract infection (UTI) is the most frequent serious bacterial infection in neonates. Approximately 10–20% of febrile episodes in infants younger than 60 days are attributed to UTIs (1) (2), making them a leading cause of hospitalization in this age group. In the United States alone, over 20,000 children under the age of 1 year are hospitalized annually for UTIs (3). In UTIs of infants older than 28 days, intravenous (IV), antibiotics are not always required : oral and parenteral treatments have demonstrated comparable efficacy, and the parenteral phase is usually limited to less than 4 days. (4). According to guidelines, antibiotic selection should be tailored based on local antimicrobial resistance patterns. The 2024 French guidelines recommend initial hospitalization with intravenous therapy for infants < 3 months. No recommendations are provided regarding oral step- down therapy, and empirical oral antibiotics at diagnosis are not advised (5). Prolonged IV antibiotic therapy, is generally reserved for high risk situations (initial sepsis, uropathy, bacteremia), or UTI caused by an Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organism, when oral therapy is not feasible (6). In clinical practice, it is essential to determine the optimal time to switch from intravenous to oral antibiotic treatment. Insufficient treatment of UTIs increases the risk of recurrence, urosepsis (7), and long-term complications such as renal scarring. At this age, intravenous treatment cannot be administered on an outpatient basis and requires hospitalization. Shortening the duration of IV therapy offers several advantages: it reduces the risk of complication related to intravenous lines and medications -related adverse events (8); it limits disruption to parent-infant bonding (9), it decreases the length of hospital stay, thereby increasing bed availability and reducing healthcare costs (10). A recent systematic review (2022) concluded that shorter IV antibiotic courses (≤ 7 days in cases of bacteremia and < 4 days without bacteremia) are appropriate for managing urinary tract infections (UTIs) in infants under 3 months of age, without meningitis, or sepsis (11). For neonates younger than 28 days, evidence-based recommendations on the optimal duration of IV antibiotic therapy are lacking. Current European, American, and Asian guidelines provide no specific guidance for this age group (12–15). Although American studies report no increased 60-day recurrence risk with short IV courses (< 4 days) (7, 16), they included broader infant populations, leaving uncertainty for neonates < 28 days. Within this group, two aspects warrant attention: infants ≤ 14 days, who may present atypically, and the potential role of procalcitonin (PCT) as a severity marker(16). The present studyfocuses specifically on neonates under 28 days. Our objectives were to describe their clinical and microbiological characteristics and to assess whether criteria, established for older infants, can be safely applied to support short IV antibiotic course (< 4 days), without increasing the risk of early recurrence. Patients and Methods Page 4/17 Study design and Population We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the university Trousseau Hospital, between 2019 to 2023. Eligible participants were infants under 28 days of age who presented to the emergency department and were subsequently hospitalized with a diagnostic of UTI. UTI was defined as the presence of ≥ 10,000 leukocytes /mL in urinalysis and ≥ 10,000 CFUs/mL of a single pathogen in urine culture. Patients were identified using ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases) codes: N10 (acute tubulointerstitial nephritis) and N11 (chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis). We excluded preterm infants (< 35 weeks gestational age), meningitis or viral co-infections. Data Collection We collected demographic and clinical data included sex, age, weight, and the presence of risk factors for early neonatal bacterial UTIs. Clinical severity at presentation was assessed based on poor peripheral perfusion (skin recoloration time greater than 3 seconds, mottling, systolic blood pressure below 60 mmHg), need for fluid resuscitation, or admission to intensive care. Laboratory data was collected at the initial presentation to the emergency department and included blood culture results, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), total white blood cell count, neutrophil count, urine culture results, and bacterial identification. All patients underwent renal ultrasonography before the third day of treatment. Therapeutic data included antibiotic regimen details: route of administration, total length of hospital stay, and duration of fever following antibiotic initiation. Follow-up data encompassedprescription of antibiotic prophylaxis, voiding cystourethrography results, and vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) grading according to the International System of Radiographic Grading. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of short-course intravenous antibiotic therapy in neonates under 28 days with urinary tract infections (UTIs). A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted at the university Trousseau Hospital between 2019 and 2023, including 138 patients with culture-proven UTI. The cohort was stratified into low-risk and high-risk groups based on clinical severity, bacteremia, pyelo-ureteral dilatation, or ESBL infection. The results showed that 98% of low-risk neonates received short IV antibiotic courses without increased recurrence. Elevated procalcitonin levels were associated with clinical severity, and fever was less frequent in neonates under 14 days. The authors concluded that short IV therapy appears safe and effective for carefully selected neonates with low-risk UTI, supporting a more tailored approach to antibiotic duration. However, the study's retrospective design and single-center nature limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate, requiring prospective validation.

papers.source_body_en: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of a short IV antibiotic course (≤ 4 days) in neonates with UTI. Methods We conducted a retrospective single-center study including neonates < 28 days hospitalized for culture- proven UTI (≥ 10,000 leukocytes/mL and ≥ 10,000 CFU/mL of a single pathogen). Results A total of 138 patients were included; (82% male, median age 15.5 days). Conclusion Short-course IV antibiotic therapy followed by oral treatment appears safe and effective for carefully selected neonates under 28 days with UTI and low risk factors for severe infection. These findings support a more tailored approach to antibiotic duration in this age group and call for prospective multicenter validation. A recent systematic review (2022) concluded that shorter IV antibiotic courses (≤ 7 days in cases of bacteremia and < 4 days without bacteremia) are appropriate for managing urinary tract infections (UTIs) in infants under 3 months of age, without meningitis, or sepsis (11). Patients and Methods Page 4/17 Study design and Population We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the university Trousseau Hospital, between 2019 to 2023. Laboratory data was collected at the initial presentation to the emergency department and included blood culture results, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), total white blood cell count, neutrophil count, urine culture results, and bacterial identification. Safe and effective short-course intravenous antibiotic therapy in neonates under 28 days with urinary tract infection Mathilde Baudin Sorbonne University Jean-Daniel Delbet Sorbonne University Charlène Ferrandiz Sorbonne University Martin Auger Sorbonne University Gael Cals Sorbonne University Antoine Mouche Sorbonne University Mathie Lorrot Sorbonne University...
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究旨在评估在患有泌尿道感染(UTI)的新生儿中使用短期静脉抗生素疗程(≤4天)的可行性和安全性。方法 我们进行了一项回顾性单中心研究,纳入了住院治疗且经培养证实的泌尿道感染(≥10,000个白细胞/毫升和单一病原体≥10,000个CFU/毫升)的新生儿,年龄小于28天。结果 共纳入138名患者;(82%男性,中位年龄15.5天)。结论 对于28天以下且严重感染风险因素较低的新生儿,短期静脉抗生素治疗后使用口服治疗似乎是安全且有效的。这些发现支持对该年龄段患者抗生素疗程采取更加个性化的策略,并呼吁进行前瞻性多中心验证。最近的一项系统综述(2022)得出结论,对于3个月以下且无脑膜炎或败血症的婴儿,较短的静脉抗生素疗程(在有菌血症的情况下≤7天,无菌血症的情况下<4天)是管理泌尿道感染(UTIs)的适当方法(11)。患者与方法 第4页/共17页 研究设计与人群 我们在2019年至2023年期间在大学Trousseau医院进行了一项回顾性队列研究研究。在最初就诊急诊科时收集了实验室数据,包括血培养结果、C反应蛋白(CRP)、降钙素原(PCT)、总白细胞计数、中性粒细胞计数、尿培养结果和细菌鉴定。对于28天以下患有泌尿道感染的新生儿,短期静脉抗生素治疗是安全且有效的。Mathilde Baudin 索邦大学 Jean-Daniel Delbet 索邦大学 Charlène Ferrandiz 索邦大学 Martin Auger 索邦大学 Gael Cals 索邦大学 Antoine Mouche 索邦大学 Mathie Lorrot 索邦大学...
